bufio.name: bufio
bufio.text: Package bufio implements buffered I/O. It wraps an io.Reader or io.Writer object, creating another object (Reader or Writer) that also implements the interface but provides buffering and some help for textual I/O.

ReadWriter.text: ReadWriter stores pointers to a Reader and a Writer.

Reader.text: Reader implements buffering for an io.Reader object.

Buffered.text: Buffered returns the number of bytes that can be read from the current buffer.

Discard.decl: func (b *Reader) Discard(n int) (discarded int, err error)
Discard.text: Discard skips the next n bytes, returning the number of bytes discarded.

Peek.text: Peek returns the next n bytes without advancing the reader.

ReadByte.text: ReadByte reads and returns a single byte.

ReadBytes.text: ReadBytes reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a slice containing the data up to and including the delimiter.

ReadLine.decl: func (b *Reader) ReadLine() (line []byte, isPrefix bool, err error)
ReadLine.text: ReadLine is a low-level line-reading primitive.

ReadRune.decl: func (b *Reader) ReadRune() (r rune, size int, err error)
ReadRune.text: ReadRune reads a single UTF-8 encoded Unicode character and returns the rune and its size in bytes.

ReadSlice.text: ReadSlice reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a slice pointing at the bytes in the buffer.

ReadString.text: ReadString reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a string containing the data up to and including the delimiter.

Reset.text: Reset discards any buffered data, resets all state, and switches the buffered reader to read from r.

Size.text: Size returns the size of the underlying buffer in bytes.

WriteTo.decl: func (b *Reader) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)

Scanner.text: Scanner provides a convenient interface for reading data such as a file of newline-delimited lines of text.

Buffer.text: Buffer controls memory allocation by the Scanner.

Bytes.text: Bytes returns the most recent token generated by a call to Scanner.Scan.

Err.text: Err returns the first non-EOF error that was encountered by the Scanner.

Scan.text: Scan advances the Scanner to the next token, which will then be available through the Scanner.Bytes or Scanner.Text method.

Split.text: Split sets the split function for the Scanner.

Text.text: Text returns the most recent token generated by a call to Scanner.Scan as a newly allocated string holding its bytes.

SplitFunc.text: SplitFunc is the signature of the split function used to tokenize the input.

Writer.text: Writer implements buffering for an io.Writer object.

Available.text: Available returns how many bytes are unused in the buffer.

AvailableBuffer.text: AvailableBuffer returns an empty buffer with b.Available() capacity.

Buffered.text: Buffered returns the number of bytes that have been written into the current buffer.

Flush.text: Flush writes any buffered data to the underlying io.Writer.

ReadFrom.decl: func (b *Writer) ReadFrom(r io.Reader) (n int64, err error)

Reset.text: Reset discards any unflushed buffered data, clears any error, and resets b to write its output to w.

Size.text: Size returns the size of the underlying buffer in bytes.

Write.text: Write writes the contents of p into the buffer.

WriteRune.decl: func (b *Writer) WriteRune(r rune) (size int, err error)
WriteRune.text: WriteRune writes a single Unicode code point, returning the number of bytes written and any error.

NewReadWriter.text: NewReadWriter allocates a new ReadWriter that dispatches to r and w.

NewReader.text: NewReader returns a new Reader whose buffer has the default size.

NewReaderSize.text: NewReaderSize returns a new Reader whose buffer has at least the specified size.

NewScanner.text: NewScanner returns a new Scanner to read from r.

NewWriter.text: NewWriter returns a new Writer whose buffer has the default size.

NewWriterSize.text: NewWriterSize returns a new Writer whose buffer has at least the specified size.

ScanBytes.decl: func ScanBytes(data []byte, atEOF bool) (advance int, token []byte, err error)
ScanBytes.text: ScanBytes is a split function for a Scanner that returns each byte as a token.

ScanLines.decl: func ScanLines(data []byte, atEOF bool) (advance int, token []byte, err error)
ScanLines.text: ScanLines is a split function for a Scanner that returns each line of text, stripped of any trailing end-of-line marker.

ScanRunes.decl: func ScanRunes(data []byte, atEOF bool) (advance int, token []byte, err error)
ScanRunes.text: ScanRunes is a split function for a Scanner that returns each UTF-8-encoded rune as a token.

ScanWords.decl: func ScanWords(data []byte, atEOF bool) (advance int, token []byte, err error)
ScanWords.text: ScanWords is a split function for a Scanner that returns each space-separated word of text, with surrounding spaces deleted.

ErrFinalToken.text: ErrFinalToken is a special sentinel error value.

bytes.name: bytes
bytes.text: Package bytes implements functions for the manipulation of byte slices.

Buffer.text: A Buffer is a variable-sized buffer of bytes with Buffer.Read and Buffer.Write methods.

Available.text: Available returns how many bytes are unused in the buffer.

AvailableBuffer.text: AvailableBuffer returns an empty buffer with b.Available() capacity.

Bytes.text: Bytes returns a slice of length b.Len() holding the unread portion of the buffer.

Cap.text: Cap returns the capacity of the buffer's underlying byte slice, that is, the total space allocated for the buffer's data.

Grow.text: Grow grows the buffer's capacity, if necessary, to guarantee space for another n bytes.

Len.text: Len returns the number of bytes of the unread portion of the buffer; b.Len() == len(b.Bytes()).

Next.text: Next returns a slice containing the next n bytes from the buffer, advancing the buffer as if the bytes had been returned by Buffer.Read.

Peek.text: Peek returns the next n bytes without advancing the buffer.

Read.text: Read reads the next len(p) bytes from the buffer or until the buffer is drained.

ReadByte.text: ReadByte reads and returns the next byte from the buffer.

ReadBytes.text: ReadBytes reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a slice containing the data up to and including the delimiter.

ReadFrom.decl: func (b *Buffer) ReadFrom(r io.Reader) (n int64, err error)
ReadFrom.text: ReadFrom reads data from r until EOF and appends it to the buffer, growing the buffer as needed.

ReadRune.decl: func (b *Buffer) ReadRune() (r rune, size int, err error)
ReadRune.text: ReadRune reads and returns the next UTF-8-encoded Unicode code point from the buffer.

ReadString.decl: func (b *Buffer) ReadString(delim byte) (line string, err error)
ReadString.text: ReadString reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a string containing the data up to and including the delimiter.

Reset.text: Reset resets the buffer to be empty, but it retains the underlying storage for use by future writes.

String.text: String returns the contents of the unread portion of the buffer as a string.

Truncate.text: Truncate discards all but the first n unread bytes from the buffer but continues to use the same allocated storage.

UnreadByte.text: UnreadByte unreads the last byte returned by the most recent successful read operation that read at least one byte.

UnreadRune.text: UnreadRune unreads the last rune returned by Buffer.ReadRune.

Write.text: Write appends the contents of p to the buffer, growing the buffer as needed.

WriteByte.text: WriteByte appends the byte c to the buffer, growing the buffer as needed.

WriteRune.decl: func (b *Buffer) WriteRune(r rune) (n int, err error)
WriteRune.text: WriteRune appends the UTF-8 encoding of Unicode code point r to the buffer, returning the number of bytes written and a nil error.

WriteString.decl: func (b *Buffer) WriteString(s string) (n int, err error)
WriteString.text: WriteString appends the contents of s to the buffer, growing the buffer as needed.

WriteTo.decl: func (b *Buffer) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)
WriteTo.text: WriteTo writes data to w until the buffer is drained or an error occurs.

Reader.text: A Reader implements the io.Reader, io.ReaderAt, io.WriterTo, io.Seeker, io.ByteScanner, and io.RuneScanner interfaces by reading from a byte slice.

Len.text: Len returns the number of bytes of the unread portion of the slice.

ReadAt.decl: func (r *Reader) ReadAt(b []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)

ReadRune.decl: func (r *Reader) ReadRune() (ch rune, size int, err error)

Reset.text: Reset resets the Reader to be reading from b.

Seek.decl: func (r *Reader) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)

Size.text: Size returns the original length of the underlying byte slice.

UnreadByte.text: UnreadByte complements Reader.ReadByte in implementing the io.ByteScanner interface.

UnreadRune.text: UnreadRune complements Reader.ReadRune in implementing the io.RuneScanner interface.

WriteTo.decl: func (r *Reader) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)

Clone.text: Clone returns a copy of b[:len(b)].

Compare.text: Compare returns an integer comparing two byte slices lexicographically.

Contains.text: Contains reports whether subslice is within b.

ContainsAny.text: ContainsAny reports whether any of the UTF-8-encoded code points in chars are within b.

ContainsFunc.decl: func ContainsFunc(b []byte, f func(rune) bool) bool
ContainsFunc.text: ContainsFunc reports whether any of the UTF-8-encoded code points r within b satisfy f(r).

ContainsRune.text: ContainsRune reports whether the rune is contained in the UTF-8-encoded byte slice b.

Count.text: Count counts the number of non-overlapping instances of sep in s.

Cut.decl: func Cut(s, sep []byte) (before, after []byte, found bool)
Cut.text: Cut slices s around the first instance of sep, returning the text before and after sep.

CutLast.decl: func CutLast(s, sep []byte) (before, after []byte, found bool)
CutLast.text: CutLast slices s around the last instance of sep, returning the text before and after sep.

CutPrefix.text: CutPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix byte slice and reports whether it found the prefix.

CutSuffix.text: CutSuffix returns s without the provided ending suffix byte slice and reports whether it found the suffix.

Equal.text: Equal reports whether a and b are the same length and contain the same bytes.

EqualFold.text: EqualFold reports whether s and t, interpreted as UTF-8 strings, are equal under simple Unicode case-folding, which is a more general form of case-insensitivity.

Fields.text: Fields interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

FieldsFunc.text: FieldsFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

FieldsFuncSeq.decl: func FieldsFuncSeq(s []byte, f func(rune) bool) iter.Seq[[]byte]
FieldsFuncSeq.text: FieldsFuncSeq returns an iterator over subslices of s split around runs of Unicode code points satisfying f(c).

FieldsSeq.text: FieldsSeq returns an iterator over subslices of s split around runs of whitespace characters, as defined by unicode.IsSpace.

HasPrefix.text: HasPrefix reports whether the byte slice s begins with prefix.

HasSuffix.text: HasSuffix reports whether the byte slice s ends with suffix.

Index.text: Index returns the index of the first instance of sep in s, or -1 if sep is not present in s.

IndexAny.text: IndexAny interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded Unicode code points.

IndexByte.text: IndexByte returns the index of the first instance of c in b, or -1 if c is not present in b.

IndexFunc.decl: func IndexFunc(s []byte, f func(r rune) bool) int
IndexFunc.text: IndexFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

IndexRune.text: IndexRune interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

Join.text: Join concatenates the elements of s to create a new byte slice.

LastIndex.text: LastIndex returns the index of the last instance of sep in s, or -1 if sep is not present in s.

LastIndexAny.text: LastIndexAny interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded Unicode code points.

LastIndexByte.text: LastIndexByte returns the index of the last instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

LastIndexFunc.decl: func LastIndexFunc(s []byte, f func(r rune) bool) int
LastIndexFunc.text: LastIndexFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

Lines.text: Lines returns an iterator over the newline-terminated lines in the byte slice s.

Map.decl: func Map(mapping func(r rune) rune, s []byte) []byte
Map.text: Map returns a copy of the byte slice s with all its characters modified according to the mapping function.

NewBuffer.text: NewBuffer creates and initializes a new Buffer using buf as its initial contents.

NewBufferString.text: NewBufferString creates and initializes a new Buffer using string s as its initial contents.

NewReader.text: NewReader returns a new Reader reading from b.

Repeat.text: Repeat returns a new byte slice consisting of count copies of b.

Replace.decl: func Replace(s, old, new []byte, n int) []byte
Replace.text: Replace returns a copy of the slice s with the first n non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.

ReplaceAll.text: ReplaceAll returns a copy of the slice s with all non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.

Runes.text: Runes interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.

Split.text: Split slices s into all subslices separated by sep and returns a slice of the subslices between those separators.

SplitAfter.text: SplitAfter slices s into all subslices after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those subslices.

SplitAfterN.text: SplitAfterN slices s into subslices after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those subslices.

SplitAfterSeq.text: SplitAfterSeq returns an iterator over subslices of s split after each instance of sep.

SplitN.text: SplitN slices s into subslices separated by sep and returns a slice of the subslices between those separators.

SplitSeq.text: SplitSeq returns an iterator over all subslices of s separated by sep.

Title.text: Title treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all Unicode letters that begin words mapped to their title case.

ToLower.text: ToLower returns a copy of the byte slice s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case.

ToLowerSpecial.text: ToLowerSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their lower case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

ToTitle.text: ToTitle treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their title case.

ToTitleSpecial.text: ToTitleSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their title case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

ToUpper.text: ToUpper returns a copy of the byte slice s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case.

ToUpperSpecial.text: ToUpperSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their upper case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

ToValidUTF8.text: ToValidUTF8 treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with each run of bytes representing invalid UTF-8 replaced with the bytes in replacement, which may be empty.

Trim.text: Trim returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and trailing UTF-8-encoded code points contained in cutset.

TrimFunc.decl: func TrimFunc(s []byte, f func(r rune) bool) []byte
TrimFunc.text: TrimFunc returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and trailing UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

TrimLeft.text: TrimLeft returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading UTF-8-encoded code points contained in cutset.

TrimLeftFunc.decl: func TrimLeftFunc(s []byte, f func(r rune) bool) []byte
TrimLeftFunc.text: TrimLeftFunc treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

TrimPrefix.text: TrimPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string.

TrimRight.text: TrimRight returns a subslice of s by slicing off all trailing UTF-8-encoded code points that are contained in cutset.

TrimRightFunc.decl: func TrimRightFunc(s []byte, f func(r rune) bool) []byte
TrimRightFunc.text: TrimRightFunc returns a subslice of s by slicing off all trailing UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

TrimSpace.text: TrimSpace returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and trailing white space, as defined by Unicode.

TrimSuffix.text: TrimSuffix returns s without the provided trailing suffix string.

ErrTooLarge.text: ErrTooLarge is passed to panic if memory cannot be allocated to store data in a buffer.

MinRead.text: MinRead is the minimum slice size passed to a Buffer.Read call by Buffer.ReadFrom.

cmp.name: cmp
cmp.text: Package cmp provides types and functions related to comparing ordered values.

Ordered.text: Ordered is a constraint that permits any ordered type: any type that supports the operators < <= >= >.

Compare.decl: func Compare[T Ordered](x, y T) int

Less.decl: func Less[T Ordered](x, y T) bool
Less.text: Less reports whether x is less than y.

Or.text: Or returns the first of its arguments that is not equal to the zero value.

context.name: context
context.text: Package context defines the Context type, which carries deadlines, cancellation signals, and other request-scoped values across API boundaries and between processes.

CancelCauseFunc.text: A CancelCauseFunc behaves like a CancelFunc but additionally sets the cancellation cause.

CancelFunc.text: A CancelFunc tells an operation to abandon its work.

Context.text: A Context carries a deadline, a cancellation signal, and other values across API boundaries.

AfterFunc.decl: func AfterFunc(ctx Context, f func()) (stop func() bool)
AfterFunc.text: AfterFunc arranges to call f in its own goroutine after ctx is canceled.

Background.text: Background returns a non-nil, empty Context.

Cause.text: Cause returns a non-nil error explaining why c was canceled.

TODO.text: TODO returns a non-nil, empty Context.

WithCancel.decl: func WithCancel(parent Context) (ctx Context, cancel CancelFunc)
WithCancel.text: WithCancel returns a derived context that points to the parent context but has a new Done channel.

WithCancelCause.decl: func WithCancelCause(parent Context) (ctx Context, cancel CancelCauseFunc)
WithCancelCause.text: WithCancelCause behaves like WithCancel but returns a CancelCauseFunc instead of a CancelFunc.

WithDeadline.decl: func WithDeadline(parent Context, d time.Time) (Context, CancelFunc)
WithDeadline.text: WithDeadline returns a derived context that points to the parent context but has the deadline adjusted to be no later than d.

WithDeadlineCause.decl: func WithDeadlineCause(parent Context, d time.Time, cause error) (Context, CancelFunc)
WithDeadlineCause.text: WithDeadlineCause behaves like WithDeadline but also sets the cause of the returned Context when the deadline is exceeded.

WithTimeout.decl: func WithTimeout(parent Context, timeout time.Duration) (Context, CancelFunc)

WithTimeoutCause.decl: func WithTimeoutCause(parent Context, timeout time.Duration, cause error) (Context, CancelFunc)
WithTimeoutCause.text: WithTimeoutCause behaves like WithTimeout but also sets the cause of the returned Context when the timeout expires.

WithValue.decl: func WithValue(parent Context, key, val any) Context
WithValue.text: WithValue returns a derived context that points to the parent Context.

WithoutCancel.text: WithoutCancel returns a derived context that points to the parent context and is not canceled when parent is canceled.

Canceled.text: Canceled is the error returned by Context.Err when the context is canceled for some reason other than its deadline passing.

DeadlineExceeded.text: DeadlineExceeded is the error returned by Context.Err when the context is canceled due to its deadline passing.

encoding/csv.name: csv
encoding/csv.text: Package csv reads and writes comma-separated values (CSV) files.

ParseError.text: A ParseError is returned for parsing errors.

Reader.text: A Reader reads records from a CSV-encoded file.

FieldPos.text: FieldPos returns the line and column corresponding to the start of the field with the given index in the slice most recently returned by Reader.Read.

InputOffset.text: InputOffset returns the input stream byte offset of the current reader position.

Read.text: Read reads one record (a slice of fields) from r.

ReadAll.text: ReadAll reads all the remaining records from r.

Writer.text: A Writer writes records using CSV encoding.

Error.text: Error reports any error that has occurred during a previous Writer.Write or Writer.Flush.

Flush.text: Flush writes any buffered data to the underlying io.Writer.

Write.text: Write writes a single CSV record to w along with any necessary quoting.

WriteAll.text: WriteAll writes multiple CSV records to w using Writer.Write and then calls Writer.Flush, returning any error from the Flush.

NewReader.text: NewReader returns a new Reader that reads from r.

NewWriter.text: NewWriter returns a new Writer that writes to w.

ErrBareQuote.text: These are the errors that can be returned in ParseError.Err.

ErrFieldCount.text: These are the errors that can be returned in ParseError.Err.

ErrQuote.text: These are the errors that can be returned in ParseError.Err.

ErrTrailingComma.text: These are the errors that can be returned in ParseError.Err.

encoding/json.name: json
encoding/json.text: Package json implements encoding and decoding of JSON as defined in RFC 7159.

Decoder.text: A Decoder reads and decodes JSON values from an input stream.

Buffered.text: Buffered returns a reader of the data remaining in the unread buffer, which may contain zero or more bytes.

Decode.text: Decode reads the next JSON-encoded value from its input and stores it in the value pointed to by v.

DisallowUnknownFields.text: DisallowUnknownFields causes the Decoder to return an error when the destination is a struct and the input contains object keys which do not match any non-ignored, exported fields in the destination.

InputOffset.text: InputOffset returns the input stream byte offset of the current decoder position.

More.text: More reports whether there is another element in the current array or object being parsed.

Token.text: Token returns the next JSON token in the input stream.

UseNumber.text: UseNumber causes the Decoder to unmarshal a number into an interface value as a Number instead of as a float64.

Delim.text: A Delim is a JSON array or object delimiter, one of [ ] { or }.

Encoder.text: An Encoder writes JSON values to an output stream.

Encode.text: Encode writes the JSON encoding of v to the stream, followed by a newline character.

SetEscapeHTML.text: SetEscapeHTML specifies whether problematic HTML characters should be escaped inside JSON quoted strings.

SetIndent.text: SetIndent instructs the encoder to format each subsequent encoded value as if indented by the package-level function Indent(dst, src, prefix, indent).

InvalidUTF8Error.text: Before Go 1.2, an InvalidUTF8Error was returned by Marshal when attempting to encode a string value with invalid UTF-8 sequences.

InvalidUnmarshalError.text: An InvalidUnmarshalError describes an invalid argument passed to Unmarshal.

Marshaler.text: Marshaler is the interface implemented by types that can marshal themselves into valid JSON.

MarshalerError.text: A MarshalerError represents an error from calling a [Marshaler.MarshalJSON] or encoding.TextMarshaler.MarshalText method.

Number.text: A Number represents a JSON number literal.

Float64.text: Float64 returns the number as a float64.

Int64.text: Int64 returns the number as an int64.

String.text: String returns the literal text of the number.

Options.text: Options are a set of options to configure the v2 "json" package to operate with v1 semantics for particular features.

RawMessage.text: RawMessage is a raw encoded JSON value.

SyntaxError.text: A SyntaxError is a description of a JSON syntax error.

Token.text: A Token holds a value of one of these types:

UnmarshalFieldError.text: An UnmarshalFieldError describes a JSON object key that led to an unexported (and therefore unwritable) struct field.

UnmarshalTypeError.text: An UnmarshalTypeError describes a JSON value that was not appropriate for a value of a specific Go type.

Unmarshaler.text: Unmarshaler is the interface implemented by types that can unmarshal a JSON description of themselves.

UnsupportedTypeError.text: An UnsupportedTypeError is returned by Marshal when attempting to encode an unsupported value type.

UnsupportedValueError.text: An UnsupportedValueError is returned by Marshal when attempting to encode an unsupported value.

CallMethodsWithLegacySemantics.text: CallMethodsWithLegacySemantics specifies that calling of type-provided marshal and unmarshal methods follow legacy semantics:

Compact.text: Compact appends to dst the JSON-encoded src with insignificant space characters elided.

DefaultOptionsV1.text: DefaultOptionsV1 is the full set of all options that define v1 semantics.

FormatByteArrayAsArray.text: FormatByteArrayAsArray specifies that a Go [N]byte is formatted as a normal Go array in contrast to the v2 default of formatting [N]byte as using binary data encoding (RFC 4648).

FormatBytesWithLegacySemantics.text: FormatBytesWithLegacySemantics specifies that handling of []~byte and [N]~byte types follow legacy semantics:

FormatDurationAsNano.text: FormatDurationAsNano specifies that a time.Duration is formatted as a JSON number representing the number of nanoseconds in contrast to the v2 default of reporting an error.

HTMLEscape.text: HTMLEscape appends to dst the JSON-encoded src with <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 characters inside string literals changed to \u003c, \u003e, \u0026, \u2028, \u2029 so that the JSON will be safe to embed inside HTML <script> tags.

Indent.decl: func Indent(dst *bytes.Buffer, src []byte, prefix, indent string) error
Indent.text: Indent appends to dst an indented form of the JSON-encoded src.

Marshal.text: Marshal returns the JSON encoding of v.

MarshalIndent.decl: func MarshalIndent(v any, prefix, indent string) ([]byte, error)
MarshalIndent.text: MarshalIndent is like Marshal but applies Indent to format the output.

MatchCaseSensitiveDelimiter.text: MatchCaseSensitiveDelimiter specifies that underscores and dashes are not to be ignored when performing case-insensitive name matching which occurs under jsonv2.MatchCaseInsensitiveNames or the `case:ignore` tag option.

MergeWithLegacySemantics.text: MergeWithLegacySemantics specifies that unmarshaling into a non-zero Go value follows legacy semantics:

NewDecoder.text: NewDecoder returns a new decoder that reads from r.

NewEncoder.text: NewEncoder returns a new encoder that writes to w.

OmitEmptyWithLegacySemantics.text: OmitEmptyWithLegacySemantics specifies that the `omitempty` tag option follows a definition of empty where a field is omitted if the Go value is false, 0, a nil pointer, a nil interface value, or any empty array, slice, map, or string.

ParseBytesWithLooseRFC4648.text: ParseBytesWithLooseRFC4648 specifies that when parsing binary data encoded as "base32" or "base64", to ignore the presence of '\r' and '\n' characters.

ParseTimeWithLooseRFC3339.text: ParseTimeWithLooseRFC3339 specifies that a time.Time parses according to loose adherence to RFC 3339.

ReportErrorsWithLegacySemantics.text: ReportErrorsWithLegacySemantics specifies that Marshal and Unmarshal should report errors with legacy semantics:

StringifyWithLegacySemantics.text: StringifyWithLegacySemantics specifies that the `string` tag option may stringify bools and string values.

Unmarshal.text: Unmarshal parses the JSON-encoded data and stores the result in the value pointed to by v.

UnmarshalArrayFromAnyLength.text: UnmarshalArrayFromAnyLength specifies that Go arrays can be unmarshaled from input JSON arrays of any length.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether data is a valid JSON encoding.

errors.name: errors
errors.text: Package errors implements functions to manipulate errors.

As.decl: func As(err error, target any) bool
As.text: As finds the first error in err's tree that matches target, and if one is found, sets target to that error value and returns true.

AsType.text: AsType finds the first error in err's tree that matches the type E, and if one is found, returns that error value and true.

Is.text: Is reports whether any error in err's tree matches target.

Join.text: Join returns an error that wraps the given errors.

New.text: New returns an error that formats as the given text.

Unwrap.text: Unwrap returns the result of calling the Unwrap method on err, if err's type contains an Unwrap method returning error.

ErrUnsupported.text: ErrUnsupported indicates that a requested operation cannot be performed, because it is unsupported.

flag.name: flag
flag.text: Package flag implements command-line flag parsing.

ErrorHandling.text: ErrorHandling defines how FlagSet.Parse behaves if the parse fails.

Flag.text: A Flag represents the state of a flag.

FlagSet.text: A FlagSet represents a set of defined flags.

Bool.decl: func (f *FlagSet) Bool(name string, value bool, usage string) *bool
Bool.text: Bool defines a bool flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

BoolFunc.decl: func (f *FlagSet) BoolFunc(name, usage string, fn func(string) error)
BoolFunc.text: BoolFunc defines a flag with the specified name and usage string without requiring values.

BoolVar.decl: func (f *FlagSet) BoolVar(p *bool, name string, value bool, usage string)
BoolVar.text: BoolVar defines a bool flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

Duration.decl: func (f *FlagSet) Duration(name string, value time.Duration, usage string) *time.Duration
Duration.text: Duration defines a time.Duration flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

DurationVar.decl: func (f *FlagSet) DurationVar(p *time.Duration, name string, value time.Duration, usage string)
DurationVar.text: DurationVar defines a time.Duration flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

ErrorHandling.text: ErrorHandling returns the error handling behavior of the flag set.

Float64.decl: func (f *FlagSet) Float64(name string, value float64, usage string) *float64
Float64.text: Float64 defines a float64 flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

Float64Var.decl: func (f *FlagSet) Float64Var(p *float64, name string, value float64, usage string)
Float64Var.text: Float64Var defines a float64 flag with specified name, default value, and usage string.

IsIdentity.text: IsIdentity reports whether the quaternion is the identity (1, 0, 0, 0).

Mirror.text: Mirror is the orientation with U and V reversed (C++ Quaternion::Mirror).

Rotate.text: Rotate expresses v in the basis (RotationU, RotationV, RotationN), as C++ Quaternion::Rotate does.

Times.text: Times is the product q b (C++ Quaternion::Times).

ToThe.text: ToThe is q, a unit quaternion, raised to the power p (C++ Quaternion::ToThe).

WithMagnitude.text: WithMagnitude is q scaled to magnitude s (C++ Quaternion::WithMagnitude).

BoundingBoxesDisjoint.decl: func (v Vector) BoundingBoxesDisjoint(amax, amin, bmax, bmin Vector) bool

ClampWithin.decl: func (v Vector) ClampWithin(minv, maxv float64) Vector

ClosestOrtho.text: ClampWithin clamps each component to [minv, maxv] (C++ Vector::ClampWithin).

ClosestPointOnLine.decl: func (v Vector) ClosestPointOnLine(p0, dp Vector) Vector
ClosestPointOnLine.text: ClosestPointOnLine is the point of the line p0 + t*dp closest to v (C++ Vector::ClosestPointOnLine).

DirectionCosineWith.text: DirectionCosineWith is the cosine of the angle between v and b (C++ Vector::DirectionCosineWith).

DistanceToLine.decl: func (v Vector) DistanceToLine(p0, dp Vector) float64
DistanceToLine.text: DistanceToLine is the distance from v to the line p0 + t*dp (C++ Vector::DistanceToLine).

DistanceToPlane.decl: func (v Vector) DistanceToPlane(normal, origin Vector) float64
DistanceToPlane.text: DistanceToPlane is v's signed distance from the plane through origin with normal (scaled by its magnitude, as C++ Vector::DistanceToPlane).

DivProjected.text: DivProjected is v's length along delta, in units of delta (C++ Vector::DivProjected).

DotInToCsys.decl: func (v Vector) DotInToCsys(u, w, n Vector) Vector
DotInToCsys.text: DotInToCsys is v's components along u, w and n (C++ Vector::DotInToCsys).

Equals.text: Equals mirrors C++ Vector::Equals with its default LENGTH_EPS tolerance (dsc.h:129).

EqualsTol.decl: func (v Vector) EqualsTol(b Vector, tol float64) bool

InPerspective.decl: func (v Vector) InPerspective(u, vv, n, origin Vector, cameraTan float64) Vector
InPerspective.text: InPerspective takes v into the csys (u, v, n) at origin, and applies the perspective of cameraTan (C++ Vector::InPerspective).

MakeMaxMin.text: MakeMaxMin expands `ptMax` and `ptMin` to include v.

NormalDir.text: NormalDir returns one of two unit vectors perpendicular to v, selected by an arbitrary but well-defined pivot rule (which=0 or 1); which=1 is which=0 crossed with v, so the pair (Normal(0), Normal(1), v) forms a right-handed orthonormal basis.

OnLineSegment.decl: func (v Vector) OnLineSegment(a, b Vector, tol float64) bool
OnLineSegment.text: OnLineSegment returns true if v lies on segment [a, b] within tol.

OutsideAndNotOn.decl: func (v Vector) OutsideAndNotOn(maxv, minv Vector) bool
OutsideAndNotOn.text: OutsideAndNotOn reports whether v lies outside the box [minv, maxv] by more than LENGTH_EPS.

Project2d.decl: func (v Vector) Project2d(u, w Vector) Point2d
Project2d.text: Project2d returns the 2-D coordinates of v expressed in the basis (u, v) of the workplane.

Project4d.text: Project4d returns the homogeneous Vector4 representation of v with unit weight.

ProjectXy.text: ProjectXy returns the 2-D coordinates of v projected onto the XY plane.

RotatedAbout.decl: func (v Vector) RotatedAbout(orig, axis Vector, theta float64) Vector
RotatedAbout.text: RotatedAbout rotates v by theta about the axis through orig (C++ Vector::RotatedAbout(orig, axis, theta)).

RotatedAroundAxis.decl: func (v Vector) RotatedAroundAxis(axis Vector, theta float64) Vector
RotatedAroundAxis.text: RotatedAroundAxis rotates v by theta about the axis through the origin (C++ Vector::RotatedAbout(axis, theta)).

ScaleOutOfCsys.decl: func (v Vector) ScaleOutOfCsys(u, w, n Vector) Vector
ScaleOutOfCsys.text: ScaleOutOfCsys takes v's components as coordinates in the (u, w, n) basis (C++ Vector::ScaleOutOfCsys).

WithMagnitude.text: WithMagnitude is v scaled to magnitude s; a zero vector stays zero (C++ Vector::WithMagnitude).

Vector4.text: Vector4 is a point in homogeneous coordinates (w*x, w*y, w*z, w) (C++ Vector4).

PerspectiveProject.text: PerspectiveProject is the point (x/w, y/w, z/w) (C++ Vector4::PerspectiveProject).

AtIntersectionOfLines.decl: func AtIntersectionOfLines(a0, a1, b0, b1 Vector) Vector
AtIntersectionOfLines.text: AtIntersectionOfLines is the point on line (a0, a1) closest to line (b0, b1), their intersection if they meet (C++ Vector::AtIntersectionOfLines, without the skew and parameter outputs).

AtIntersectionOfLinesSkew.decl: func AtIntersectionOfLinesSkew(a0, a1, b0, b1 Vector) (Vector, bool)
AtIntersectionOfLinesSkew.text: AtIntersectionOfLinesSkew is AtIntersectionOfLines, also reporting whether the lines are skew: whether the closest points on them aren't coincident (C++ Vector::AtIntersectionOfLines with skew).

AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLine.decl: func AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLine(n Vector, d float64, p0, p1 Vector) Vector
AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLine.text: AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLine is where the line through p0 and p1 meets the plane n .

AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLineParallel.decl: func AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLineParallel(n Vector, d float64, p0, p1 Vector) (Vector, bool)
AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLineParallel.text: AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLineParallel is AtIntersectionOfPlaneAndLine, also reporting whether the line and plane are parallel.

AtIntersectionOfThreePlanes.decl: func AtIntersectionOfThreePlanes(na Vector, da float64, nb Vector, db float64, nc Vector, dc float64) (Vector, bool)
AtIntersectionOfThreePlanes.text: AtIntersectionOfThreePlanes returns the point where the three planes meet, reporting parallel when they don't meet in a point.

AtIntersectionOfTwoPlanes.decl: func AtIntersectionOfTwoPlanes(n1 Vector, d1 float64, n2 Vector, d2 float64) Vector
AtIntersectionOfTwoPlanes.text: AtIntersectionOfTwoPlanes returns a point on the line where planes (n1, d1) and (n2, d2) meet.

BoundingBoxIntersectsLine.decl: func BoundingBoxIntersectsLine(amax, amin, p0, p1 Vector, asSegment bool) bool
BoundingBoxIntersectsLine.text: BoundingBoxIntersectsLine reports whether the line (or, if asSegment, the segment) p0-p1 crosses a face of the box.

ClosestPointBetweenLines.decl: func ClosestPointBetweenLines(a0, da, b0, db Vector) (ta, tb float64)
ClosestPointBetweenLines.text: ClosestPointBetweenLines computes the parameters ta, tb on the two lines (a0, da) and (b0, db) such that a0 + ta*da is the closest point on the first line to the second.

Max.text: Max is C++ std::max for doubles: b if a < b, else a.

Min.text: Min is C++ std::min for doubles: b if b < a, else a (see Max).

NewQuaternion.decl: func NewQuaternion(w, x, y, z float64) Quaternion

NewVector.decl: func NewVector(x, y, z float64) Vector

Point2dFromPolar.text: Point2dFromPolar is the point at radius r and angle a (C++ Point2d::FromPolar).

QuaternionFromAxisAngle.decl: func QuaternionFromAxisAngle(axis Vector, dtheta float64) Quaternion
QuaternionFromAxisAngle.text: QuaternionFromAxisAngle is the rotation by dtheta about axis (C++ Quaternion::From(Vector axis, double dtheta)).

QuaternionFromBasis.text: QuaternionFromBasis builds the quaternion that rotates the X axis onto u and the Y axis onto v.

Vector4Blend.decl: func Vector4Blend(a, b Vector4, t float64) Vector4
Vector4Blend.text: Vector4Blend is a*(1 - t) + b*t (C++ Vector4::Blend).

Vector4From.decl: func Vector4From(w, x, y, z float64) Vector4
Vector4From.text: Vector4From is (x, y, z, w) (C++ Vector4::From(w, x, y, z)).

Vector4FromWeighted.decl: func Vector4FromWeighted(w float64, v Vector) Vector4
Vector4FromWeighted.text: Vector4FromWeighted is v with weight w: (w*v, w) (C++ Vector4::From(w, v)).

LengthEps.text: LengthEps and VeryPositive mirror C++ LENGTH_EPS and VERY_POSITIVE (solvespace/src/defs.h:7-8).

Pi.text: Pi is math.Pi as a variable.

VeryPositive.text: LengthEps and VeryPositive mirror C++ LENGTH_EPS and VERY_POSITIVE (solvespace/src/defs.h:7-8).

github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/per.name: convert
github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/per.text: Package convert imports SolveSpace .slvs files as .spcs documents.

CycleError.text: CycleError is the error for files that link each other in a ring.

Item.text: Item is one file of a plan.

Options.text: Options say how Run treats what is there already.

Plan.text: Plan is what an import would write: every file, links before the files that link them, and the root last.

Existing.text: Existing lists the linked files whose .spcs copy exists already, for which the user chooses reuse or overwrite once.

Missing.text: Missing lists the files of the plan that can't be read.

Root.text: Root is the plan's root item.

File.decl: func File(root, dst string, overwrite bool) (*Plan, *Result, error)
File.text: File converts root and what it links to dst without asking anything: the batch conversion the command line runs.

MakePlan.text: MakePlan walks the link tree of root, which is converted to dst.

Run.text: Run converts the files of the plan, links first.

SiblingPath.text: SiblingPath is where a linked .slvs file's .spcs copy goes: beside it, with the extension changed.

ErrCancelled.text: ErrCancelled is Run's error when the user cancelled at a missing linked file.

github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/per.name: spcs
github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/per.text: Package spcs reads and writes spacesolve's own file format, .spcs, described in docs/spcs-format.md.

Encode.text: Encode writes the document as it was decoded, without regenerating it: its saved entities, mesh and shell as the file held them.

Error.text: Error is a syntax error, or a model error found while decoding, at a place in the file.

File.text: File is a parsed file: its statements in order, the header first.

LinkError.text: LinkError is SaveFile's error for a link that can't be written relative to the new file, such as one on another Windows volume.

Node.text: Node is a statement: a field, a field with an expression, or a block with statements inside.

Options.text: Options are what a save records beside the sketch; none yet.

Pos.text: Pos is a place in a file: a line and a column, both from 1.

Value.text: Value is one value of a statement: a word, or a string when Quoted.

VersionError.text: VersionError is the error for a file of a newer major version than this reader knows.

DecodeTree.text: DecodeTree is Decode for a parsed file.

Encode.text: Encode writes a sketch the caller has just regenerated, as a user interface does through its own GenerateAll.

EncodeTree.text: EncodeTree is Encode without the refresh, as a tree.

FormatReal.text: FormatReal writes v in the shortest form that reads back to the same bits: plain notation from 1e-6 up to 1e21, exponent notation outside.

Load.decl: func Load(data []byte, path string) (doc *Document, err error)
Load.text: Load is LoadFile for a file's contents, data, with links relative to path.

LoadFile.text: LoadFile opens a document: it decodes the file, loads what the sketch links, asking through link.LocateMissingFile for a missing file, and regenerates the sketch without solving.

Parse.text: Parse reads the syntax of a file.

Print.text: Print writes a tree back as text.

SaveFile.decl: func SaveFile(sk *sketch.Sketch, from, path string, o Options) error
SaveFile.text: SaveFile regenerates nothing: it writes a sketch the caller has just regenerated to path, with its links rebased from the file the sketch was in (from, or "" for a new sketch) to path.

String.text: String makes a quoted value.

ErrCancelled.text: ErrCancelled is LoadFile's error when the user cancelled loading at a missing linked file.

Extension.text: Extension is the file extension of the format, without its dot.

Version.text: Version is the major version of the format this package writes, and the newest it reads.

github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/scr.name: api
github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/scr.text:
Package api is what a script sees of a sketch: a Doc and the groups,
requests, entities, constraints and parameters in it. Those are held
by handle, so they stay valid when the sketch regenerates, and are
looked up again at every call; a Doc therefore always shows the
drawing as it is.

Lengths and coordinates are in millimetres, whatever the document's
unit, and angles in degrees. Only text typed for a value, as the
SetExpr methods take, is in the document's unit (Doc.Units), as it
is in the user interface.

A call that can't do what it was asked, because of what it was given
or of the sketch's state, panics with an error; the interpreter
reports it and goes on. What reads or writes files returns an error
instead.

The package is plain Go: a script that works can be compiled as it
is.

BrokenReference.text:
BrokenReference is something a regeneration deleted because what it
used was gone: a group whose sketch was deleted, or a constraint on a
line that was.

Constraint.text:
Constraint is a constraint of the sketch: a dimension, such as a
distance or an angle, or a relation, such as two lines being
parallel.

Comment.text: Comment is the text of a comment.

Expr.text:
Expr is the expression the constraint's value comes from, as its
label's editor shows it, or "" for a plain number.

Group.text: Group is the group the constraint is in.

Other.text:
Other is whether an angle measures the supplementary angle, or an
equal-angle constraint pairs the other angles.

Reference.text:
Reference reports whether the constraint is a reference dimension,
which measures and doesn't constrain.

Set.text:
Set gives the constraint a value, as editing its label on the
drawing does: a length in mm, an angle in degrees, a ratio. A
negative distance from a line or a plane puts the point on the
other side.

SetComment.text: SetComment changes the text of a comment.

SetExpr.text:
SetExpr gives the constraint the value of text, as typing it in its
label does: a length in the document's unit (Doc.Units), an angle in
degrees, a ratio. A plain number is stored as its value; any other
text, "25.4/2" or "wall*4" with a parameter (Doc.SetParameter), is
kept and evaluated again at each regeneration.

SetOther.text:
SetOther makes an angle measure the supplementary angle, the other
one of the two its lines make, or not; for an equal-angle
constraint it pairs the other angles. Constrain > Other
Supplementary Angle toggles it.

SetReference.text:
SetReference makes the constraint a reference dimension, or a
constraint again.

String.text:
String describes the constraint as the property browser does, with
its value if it has one: "c002-pt-pt-distance = 40".

Type.text: Type is the constraint's type, as the core package names them.

Valid.text:
Valid reports whether the constraint exists: a constraint goes when
what it constrains is deleted.

Value.text:
Value is the constraint's value as the drawing labels it: a length
in mm, an angle in degrees, a ratio.

Doc.text: Doc is a sketch: the drawing a script reads and changes.

Activate.text: Activate makes g the group that is worked in.

Active.text: Active is the group that is worked in: what is drawn goes into it.

ActiveWorkplane.text:
ActiveWorkplane is the workplane that is drawn in; it isn't Valid
when drawing freely in 3d.

Angle.decl: func (d *Doc) Angle(a, b Entity, degrees float64) Constraint
Angle.text:
Angle sets the angle in degrees between two line segments or
normals. For two lines that share an end it is the angle at that
corner.

Arc.decl: func (d *Doc) Arc(center, start, end Vec) Entity
Arc.text:
Arc adds an arc of a circle around center, from start
counter-clockwise to end, in the active workplane. The end is put
at the start's distance from the centre.

Batch.text:
Batch runs fn in one go. In the application, where each call of
this package waits for the user interface, that is much faster for
a script that makes many things, and the drawing isn't shown half
done.

BrokenReferences.text:
BrokenReferences lists what the last regeneration that deleted
something deleted, as Edit > Broken References shows it. The list
stays until a regeneration deletes something else, an undo or redo,
or ClearBrokenReferences. Undo brings the deleted items back.

Chamfer.decl: func (d *Doc) Chamfer(edges []Entity, distance float64, name string) Group
Chamfer.text:
Chamfer cuts edges of the solid so far, at distance mm from each
edge on both faces that meet there, a 45 degree chamfer where they
are square. An edge is a line segment that lies along an edge
between two flat faces and sticks out, as the copies of the sketch
at the ends of an extrusion and the lines along its sides do; or a
circle or arc where a flat face meets a cylinder square to it, as an
extruded circle's, which is cut all round by a cone. The new group
becomes active.

ChamferSolid.decl: func (d *Doc) ChamferSolid(edges []SolidEdge, distance float64, name string) Group
ChamferSolid.text:
ChamferSolid cuts edges of the solid so far, by name, at distance mm
from each edge on both faces: any straight edge between two flat
faces, such as one a Boolean made, or a circular one where a flat
face meets a cylinder, picked from Solid. The chamfer
keeps the edges' names, so it follows them when the model upstream
changes, and reports when one no longer resolves. The new group
becomes active.

ChordTolerance.text:
ChordTolerance is how closely meshes follow curves, as a percentage
of the model's size.

Circle.decl: func (d *Doc) Circle(center Vec, radius float64) Entity
Circle.text:
Circle adds a circle. In a workplane it lies in it; in 3d it is
parallel to the XY plane.

ClearBrokenReferences.text: ClearBrokenReferences empties the list BrokenReferences gives.

ClearSection.text: ClearSection turns the section view off.

Coincident.text: Coincident puts two points at the same place.

Comment.decl: func (d *Doc) Comment(at Vec, text string) Constraint
Comment.text: Comment writes text on the drawing at a place.

Constrain.decl: func (d *Doc) Constrain(t core.ConstraintType, ptA, ptB, entityA, entityB Entity, other, other2 bool) Constraint
Constrain.text:
Constrain adds a constraint of any type, as the core package names
them, on up to two points and two other entities; see the solver's
documentation for what each type takes. Give Entity{} for what a
type doesn't take.

Constraint.text:
Constraint is the constraint with a description as the property
browser shows it: "c002-pt-pt-distance" or just "c002".

Cubic.decl: func (d *Doc) Cubic(p0, p1, p2, p3 Vec) Entity
Cubic.text:
Cubic adds a cubic Bézier curve from p0 to p3, with the control
points p1 and p2.

DeleteParameter.text:
DeleteParameter removes a parameter. One that an expression names
is not removed, and the error says what names it.

Diameter.decl: func (d *Doc) Diameter(circle Entity, v float64) Constraint
Diameter.text: Diameter sets the diameter of a circle or an arc.

Distance.decl: func (d *Doc) Distance(a, b Entity, v float64) Constraint
Distance.text:
Distance sets the distance between two points, or from a point to a
line segment, a workplane or a face; either may come first. A
negative distance from a line, a workplane or a face is on the
other side of it.

Entity.text: Entity is the entity with a handle.

Equal.text:
Equal makes two line segments as long as each other, two circles or
arcs of the same radius, or a line segment as long as an arc.

Export.text:
Export writes the sketch in the format the file's extension names:
the mesh of the solid (.stl, .obj, ...), the view (.svg, .dxf, .pdf,
...), the surfaces of the solid (.step), or a picture as Render
makes it (.png).

ExportAs.decl: func (d *Doc) ExportAs(kind ExportKind, path string) (err error)
ExportAs.text:
ExportAs is Export for a format that can hold several things, such
as a wireframe in a .dxf or a .step.

ExprErrors.text:
ExprErrors lists the expressions on constraints and group values
that the last regeneration could not evaluate, each with why; the
values they drive keep their last good value.

Extrude.decl: func (d *Doc) Extrude(depth float64, name string) Group
Extrude.text:
Extrude makes a solid of the active group's sketch by extruding it
by depth along the normal of its workplane, or against it for a
negative depth. The depth is where the extrusion starts, as when it
is dragged; constrain a point of it to keep it. The new group
becomes active.

Fillet.decl: func (d *Doc) Fillet(edges []Entity, radius float64, name string) Group
Fillet.text:
Fillet rounds edges of the solid so far with radius mm: line segments
along edges between two flat faces, as the copies of the sketch at
the ends of an extrusion and the lines along its sides are. Each edge
must end at corners of three flat faces. An edge that sticks out is
rounded off, and one that goes in, as a pocket's, is filled. Two
rounded edges that meet at a corner are mitred, their cylinders
meeting along an ellipse, when the faces lie alike about them; three
get a sphere. A circle or arc where a flat face meets a cylinder
square to it, as an extruded circle's, a hole's rim or a boss's foot,
is rounded all round by a torus. The faces a fillet makes are exact cylinders, spheres and
tori, and their edges have names. The new group becomes active.

FilletSolid.decl: func (d *Doc) FilletSolid(edges []SolidEdge, radius float64, name string) Group
FilletSolid.text:
FilletSolid rounds edges of the solid so far, by name, with radius
mm, as Fillet does: any straight edge between two flat faces, such
as one a Boolean made, or a circular one, picked from Solid. The fillet
keeps the names, so it follows the edges when the model upstream
changes. The new group becomes active.

Free3D.text: Free3D draws freely in 3d, in no workplane, in the active group.

Group.text:
Group is the group with a name, or with a description as the
property browser shows it: "g003-extrude" or just "g003". Check
Valid if there may be none.

Groups.text: Groups are the groups, in order, without the references.

Helix.decl: func (d *Doc) Helix(axis Entity, degrees, length float64, name string) Group
Helix.text:
Helix makes a solid of the active group's sketch by sweeping it
around a line segment by an angle in degrees while moving it along
the segment's direction by length, as a screw thread does: 360 and a
length of the pitch make one turn. A negative angle turns the other
way. The new group becomes active.

Horizontal.text:
Horizontal makes a line segment, or two points, horizontal in the
active workplane.

Host.text: Host is the program around the sketch.

Image.decl: func (d *Doc) Image(path string, at Vec, height float64) Entity
Image.text:
Image adds a picture from a file in the active workplane, for
tracing: its bottom left corner at at, height high and as wide as
the picture's proportions make it. It is construction, as the
interface makes it.

Lathe.decl: func (d *Doc) Lathe(axis Entity, name string) Group
Lathe.text:
Lathe makes a solid of the active group's sketch by turning it all
the way around a line segment. The new group becomes active.

Length.decl: func (d *Doc) Length(line Entity, v float64) Constraint
Length.text: Length sets the length of a line segment.

Line.text:
Line adds a line segment from a to b. In a workplane the points are
put in it.

Link.decl: func (d *Doc) Link(path, name string) (g Group, err error)
Link.text:
Link brings in another sketch file, a STEP file, or an STL file, as
a group, named after the file if name is empty. The new group becomes
active. A STEP file comes in as a reference mesh, its faces
tessellated, with a point at each vertex and at the centre of each
circular edge for constraints to use; LinkInfo and LinkProblem say
what was read.

Load.text: Load replaces the sketch by the one in a .spcs file.

Lock.text: Lock keeps a point where it is.

Loft.decl: func (d *Doc) Loft(from, to Group, name string) Group
Loft.text:
Loft joins the closed loops of two sketches in workplanes, from and
to, with ruled faces, curve by curve, and closes the ends with the
sketches' planes: each loop must be one closed loop, with as many
curves as the other; a circle counts as four. The solid joins the
solid so far as an extrusion's does. The new group becomes active.

Measure.text:
Measure measures what it is given, as the description of the
selection and Analyze > Measure do, without adding a constraint: one
line segment (its length) or circle (its radius); two points; a point
and a circle, line segment or plane face; two lines, normals or
plane faces (their angle in degrees); or two points and a line to
project their distance on. Lengths are in mm.

Midpoint.text: Midpoint puts a point at the middle of a line segment.

Mirror.decl: func (d *Doc) Mirror(plane Entity, name string) Group
Mirror.text:
Mirror reflects the active group in plane, a workplane or a planar
face: its entities are copied reflected, and its solid is reflected
and joined with the original, combined with the model before it as
the active group's solid is, so a mirrored hole is cut too. The
copies follow the plane when it moves. The new group becomes
active; SetKeepOriginal(false) leaves the original out of the
solid.

MmPerUnit.text:
MmPerUnit is the size in mm of the unit the user interface shows
lengths in.

NewWorkplane.decl: func (d *Doc) NewWorkplane(origin, u, v Vec) Entity
NewWorkplane.text:
NewWorkplane adds a workplane through origin, with u to its right
and v up, to a group drawn freely in 3d.

On.text:
On puts a point on a line segment, a circle or an arc, a workplane
or a face.

Origin.text: Origin is the point at the origin.

Parallel.text: Parallel makes two line segments or normals parallel.

Parameter.decl: func (d *Doc) Parameter(name string) (p Parameter, ok bool)
Parameter.text:
Parameter returns the parameter named name, and whether there is
one.

ParameterUsers.text:
ParameterUsers describes what names the parameter: other
parameters, constraints and group values.

Parameters.text:
Parameters lists the parameter table, in the order the parameters
were made.

Perpendicular.text: Perpendicular makes two line segments or normals perpendicular.

Point.text: Point adds a datum point at p.

Polyline.text:
Polyline adds the line segments through points, each starting
where the last ended, and back to the first if closed.

Radius.decl: func (d *Doc) Radius(circle Entity, v float64) Constraint
Radius.text:
Radius sets the radius of a circle or an arc; the drawing shows the
dimension as a radius.

Rect.text:
Rect adds a rectangle with the corners a and b and sides along the
active workplane's axes: four line segments, joined, two horizontal
and two vertical, returned starting with the bottom one and going
around counter-clockwise. It makes the same requests and constraints
as the interface's rectangle tool dragged from the top left corner.

Redo.text: Redo does again what Undo took back.

Regen.text: Regen regenerates the whole sketch and solves it.

RenameParameter.text:
RenameParameter renames a parameter, and rewrites every expression
that names it.

Render.decl: func (d *Doc) Render(path string, width, height int, view string) (err error)
Render.text:
Render draws the sketch into a PNG file of width by height pixels,
fitted to it and seen from "top", "bottom", "left", "right",
"front", "back" or "isometric".

Request.text:
Request is the request with a description as the property browser
shows it: "r004-line-segment" or just "r004".

Revolve.decl: func (d *Doc) Revolve(axis Entity, degrees float64, name string) Group
Revolve.text:
Revolve makes a solid of the active group's sketch by turning it by
an angle in degrees around a line segment. The new group becomes
active.

Rotate.decl: func (d *Doc) Rotate(n int, center, axis Entity, degrees float64, name string) Group
Rotate.text:
Rotate repeats the model so far n times, each turned by an angle in
degrees from the one before, about an axis through a point: the
direction of a line segment or of a normal, or, with no axis
(Entity{}), the normal of the active workplane. The new group
becomes active.

RunCommand.text:
RunCommand runs a command of the main menu, as choosing it does:
"View > Zoom To Fit", or the entry's own name, "Zoom To Fit", when
only one entry has it. A host with no window, such as spacesolve-cli,
has no menu to run it from, and it is an error.

Save.text:
Save regenerates the sketch and writes it to a .spcs file. A
SolveSpace model (.slvs) is not written.

Section.text:
Section is the section view's state and its cut of the active
group's solid.

Select.text: Select selects entities on the drawing, and nothing else.

SelectedConstraints.text: SelectedConstraints are the constraints selected on the drawing.

Selection.text:
Selection is what is selected on the drawing, but for the
constraints.

SetChordTolerance.text:
SetChordTolerance sets how closely meshes follow curves, as a
percentage of the model's size (0.1 unless set; smaller is finer and
slower), and regenerates everything. In the application it is the
setting Configuration shows; scripts that check volumes against a
formula use a fine one.

SetParameter.text:
SetParameter gives the parameter name the expression expr, and adds
it to the table if there is none:
SetParameter("wall", "2.5"), then SetParameter("bore", "wall*4").
An expression that names an unknown parameter, makes a cycle or has
no value is refused, and the table is left as it was. What uses the
parameter regenerates.

SetSection.decl: func (d *Doc) SetSection(plane Entity, offset string, flip bool)
SetSection.text:
SetSection turns the section view on: the solid is drawn cut by a
plane parallel to plane, a workplane or a planar face, offset along
its normal (a number or an expression in the document's unit, ""
for none), the side the normal points to taken away, or the other
side with flip. It is a way of looking, as View > Section View is:
not saved and not undone. Render draws it too.

SetUnits.text:
SetUnits makes u the document's unit, keeping every size, as View >
Dimension Units does: a length expression is rewritten to give the
same length in u, "(1/4)*25.4" for "1/4" from inches to mm. It
returns the parameters that lengths are computed from, which now
count in u.

SetWorkplane.text:
SetWorkplane makes wp the workplane that is drawn in, in the active
group.

Shell.decl: func (d *Doc) Shell(faces []Entity, thick float64, name string) Group
Shell.text:
Shell hollows the solid so far to walls thick mm, open where the faces
are taken away: face entities, as Group.Faces gives an extrusion's.
This version hollows solids of flat faces, and refuses a thickness at
which walls meet. The faces of the cavity have names. The new group
becomes active.

ShellSolid.decl: func (d *Doc) ShellSolid(faces []SolidFace, thick float64, name string) Group
ShellSolid.text:
ShellSolid hollows the solid so far as Shell does, taking away faces
picked from Solid, such as one a Boolean or a loft made.

Sketch3D.text: Sketch3D adds a group to draw in freely in 3d, and makes it active.

SketchAt.decl: func (d *Doc) SketchAt(origin Entity, u, v Vec, name string) Group
SketchAt.text:
SketchAt adds a group to draw in, in a workplane through a point,
with u to its right and v up; the nearest directions square to each
other are taken. The new group becomes active.

SketchIn.decl: func (d *Doc) SketchIn(wp Entity, name string) Group
SketchIn.text:
SketchIn adds a group to draw in, in a workplane like wp: one of
the reference workplanes, a workplane that was drawn, or the
workplane of another group. The new group becomes active, and its
workplane the one drawn in.

Split.decl: func (d *Doc) Split(a, b Entity, near Vec)
Split.text:
Split cuts two curves where they cross, or a curve at a point on it,
as Sketch > Split Curves at Intersection does. Of several crossings
it takes the one nearest near. It is its own step of undo.

String.text: String describes the document.

Sweep.text:
Sweep moves the closed loops of the active group, a sketch in a
workplane, along path, line segments and arcs joined end to end and
meeting tangent, as a pipe follows its bends. The sweep starts at
the end of the path nearest the sketch's plane, with the sketch
where it is drawn, and keeps its attitude to the path. The new group
becomes active.

Symmetric.decl: func (d *Doc) Symmetric(a, b, about Entity) Constraint
Symmetric.text:
Symmetric makes two points mirror images of each other about a
workplane or a line segment; with no such thing (Entity{}), about
the axis of the active workplane they are across.

Tangent.text:
Tangent makes an arc or a cubic tangent to a line segment, or to
another arc or cubic, where they share an end.

TangentArc.decl: func (d *Doc) TangentArc(point Entity, radius float64, trim bool)
TangentArc.text:
TangentArc rounds the corner at a point where two line segments or
arcs of the active workplane meet, with an arc tangent to both, as
Sketch > Tangent Arc at Point does. radius 0 lets the program choose
it. With trim, the two are cut back to the arc; without, they become
construction and trimmed copies are added. It is its own step of
undo.

Text.decl: func (d *Doc) Text(text, font string, at Vec, height float64) Entity
Text.text:
Text adds text in a TrueType font in the active workplane, its
bottom left corner at at, and height high; it is as wide as the
font makes it. font is the name of a font file the program knows,
as the text window lists them, or "" for the one built in.

Thread.decl: func (d *Doc) Thread(circle Entity, o ThreadOptions) (g Group)
Thread.text:
Thread makes a screw thread on a circle or an arc, about its axis
and from its plane, as New Group > Screw Thread does: four groups,
a sketch and a lathe that turn the part down (or bore it), and a
ridge sketch and a helix that sweeps it. It returns the helix group,
which becomes active; its Check says whether the solid came out
sound at the chord tolerance of the moment.

Translate.decl: func (d *Doc) Translate(n int, delta Vec, name string) Group
Translate.text:
Translate repeats the model so far n times, each a step of delta
from the one before. The new group becomes active.

UV.text: UV is the point at (u, v) in the active workplane.

Undo.text:
Undo takes back the last step: in a console, what the last line
that changed the sketch did.

Units.text:
Units is the document's unit of length: what lengths typed as text,
in Constraint.SetExpr and Group.SetExpr and in the user interface,
are in. Every other length this package takes or gives is in mm.

Unsaved.text: Unsaved reports whether the sketch changed since it was saved.

Vertical.text:
Vertical makes a line segment, or two points, vertical in the
active workplane.

With.text:
With runs fn on the sketch itself, for what this package has no
call for; see the sketch and core packages. The sketch and what is
got from it must not be kept after fn returns. The active group is
taken to have changed.

Workplane.text:
Workplane is one of the three reference workplanes: "XY", "YZ" or
"ZX".

Entity.text:
Entity is something on the drawing: a point, a line segment, a
circle, an arc, a curve, a workplane, a normal, a face. What is
drawn makes several: a line segment is an entity and so are its two
ends.

Center.text:
Center is the centre of a circle or an arc, or the origin of a
workplane.

Construction.text:
Construction reports whether the entity is construction geometry,
which helps to draw but makes no part of the outline.

Delete.text:
Delete deletes what was drawn to make the entity, and the
constraints on it.

Dir.text:
Dir is the direction of a line segment, from its start to its end,
or of a normal; it isn't a unit vector for a line.

End.text: End is the other end of a line segment, an arc or a cubic.

Free.text:
Free is how much of the entity its group's constraints fix, as the
drawing colours it: sketch.FreedomFixed when it is fully constrained,
sketch.FreedomPartly when some of it can still move,
sketch.FreedomFree when nothing holds it, and sketch.FreedomUnknown
when its group did not solve. Parameters from earlier groups, such
as a workplane's, count as fixed.

Group.text: Group is the group the entity is in.

Kind.text:
Kind names what the entity is: "point", "line", "circle", "arc",
"cubic", "workplane", "normal", "face", ...

Length.text: Length is the length of a line segment, an arc or a circle.

MoveTo.text:
MoveTo puts a point at p, as dragging it there does: the solver
then moves it as the constraints require.

Normal.text: Normal is the normal of a circle, an arc or a workplane.

Points.text:
Points are the points of the entity: the ends of a line, the centre
and the ends of an arc, the centre of a circle, the control points
of a cubic, the origin of a workplane. A point has itself.

Pos.text: Pos is where a point is.

Radius.text: Radius is the radius of a circle or an arc.

Request.text:
Request is what was drawn to make the entity; it isn't Valid for an
entity a group made, such as the copies an extrusion makes.

SetConstruction.text: SetConstruction makes what was drawn construction geometry, or not.

SetRadius.text:
SetRadius gives a circle a radius, as dragging it does; constrain
it with Diameter or Radius to keep it.

Start.text: Start is the first end of a line segment, an arc or a cubic.

String.text: String describes the entity, as "line r004-line-segment".

Type.text: Type is the entity's type, as the core package names them.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the entity exists.

Group.text:
Group is a group of the sketch: a drawing in a workplane or in 3d,
or a step that makes a solid from the group before it, as an
extrusion does.

Bounds.text:
Bounds are the corners of the box around the model up to and with
this group.

Check.text:
Check checks the solid of the model up to and with this group: it
reports naked and self-intersecting edges, whether the Boolean
failed, the face and triangle counts, and the volume, centre of mass
and bounding box, in mm. Report.Sound() says whether the solid is
closed, does not cross itself, and came from a Boolean that worked;
Report.Summary() says it in words. Analyze > Check Solid shows the
same report.

Conflicts.text:
Conflicts lists the constraints that keep the group from solving,
as its solve-failure screen does, any one of which could be removed
to fix it; none when the group solved.

Delete.text: Delete deletes the group and what depends on it.

DependsOn.text:
DependsOn lists the groups this group refers to, in history order:
the group it extrudes or copies, the workplane it is drawn in, and the
groups whose entities its sketch and constraints name. The references
are left out.

Distance.text: Distance is a chamfer's distance in mm.

Dof.text: Dof is how many degrees of freedom the group's constraints leave.

Edges.text:
Edges are the edges a chamfer cuts or a fillet rounds, or the path a
sweep follows.

Entities.text:
Entities are the group's entities, the points and normals among
them.

Expr.text:
Expr is the expression one of the group's values comes from, or ""
for a plain number.

Faces.text:
Faces are the planar faces this group made, which constraints and
the section view can refer to.

KeepOriginal.text:
KeepOriginal reports whether a mirror's solid has the original as
well as the reflection.

Kind.text:
Kind names what the group is: "sketch-in-plane", "sketch-in-3d",
"extrude", "lathe", "revolve", "helix", "rotate", "translate",
"mirror", "chamfer", "sweep", "fillet", "loft", "shell" or "link".

LeftOut.text:
LeftOut says why the group is left out of the model, or "" if it is
in: "suppressed" for a group suppressed whole, or "uses g004-sketch,
which is suppressed" for one that uses such a group. A group left out
has no entities and no solid of its own, and can't be made active.

LinkInfo.text:
LinkInfo describes the file a link group links, a line each, as the
group's screen shows it: for a STEP file its schema and unit, how
many shapes, faces and triangles it gave, and the chord tolerance it
was tessellated to. A sketch or STL file gives none.

LinkProblem.text:
LinkProblem says what of the file a link group links could not be
read, such as the faces of a STEP file on a kind of surface the
reader does not support, or that the file holds no solid it can
read; "" when all of it was.

Mesh.text:
Mesh is the triangle mesh of the model up to and with this group.
It is the sketch's own, and is replaced when the sketch
regenerates.

MoveBefore.text:
MoveBefore moves the group in the history to just before other, as
one undo step. A move that would put a group ahead of a group it
uses is refused with an error naming both, and nothing changes:
an extrusion can't move before its sketch, nor a sketch after its
extrusion. The references stay first.

MoveToEnd.text:
MoveToEnd moves the group to the end of the history, as MoveBefore
does.

Param.text:
Param is the group's i-th parameter: for an extrusion, 0 to 2 are
the vector to its middle; for a step and repeat translating, the step; for a
revolve or a step and repeat rotating, 3 is the angle in radians.

Plane.text: Plane is the workplane or face a mirror reflects in.

Problem.text:
Problem says what the last regeneration found wrong with the
group's input, as an edge a chamfer can't cut or a sweep path with
a corner, or "" when there is nothing; a group with a problem adds
no solid.

Radius.text: Radius is a fillet's radius in mm.

Requests.text: Requests are what was drawn in the group.

SetColor.decl: func (g Group) SetColor(red, green, blue int)
SetColor.text:
SetColor colours the group's solid; each of red, green and blue is
0 to 255.

SetCombine.text:
SetCombine says how the group's solid combines with the solid so
far: Union, Difference, Intersection or Assemble.

SetCopies.text: SetCopies is how many copies a step and repeat makes.

SetDistance.text:
SetDistance sets a chamfer's distance in mm; SetExpr with
sketch.GroupPitch gives it an expression in the document's unit.

SetExpr.decl: func (g Group) SetExpr(value sketch.GroupValue, expr string) (err error)
SetExpr.text:
SetExpr gives one of the group's values text, as typing it on the
group screen does: sketch.GroupCopies for a step and repeat,
sketch.GroupPitch for a helix's fixed pitch, a length in the
document's unit (Doc.Units), sketch.GroupScale for a link. A plain
number is stored as its value; any other text is kept and evaluated
again at each regeneration.

SetKeepOriginal.text:
SetKeepOriginal has a mirror's solid keep the original beside the
reflection, or not, which leaves the reflection alone.

SetRadius.text:
SetRadius sets a fillet's radius in mm; SetExpr with
sketch.GroupPitch gives it an expression in the document's unit.

SetSuppress.text:
SetSuppress leaves the group's solid out of the model with
SuppressSolid; the whole group, its sketch, solve and solid, with
SuppressWhole, which also leaves out every group that uses it; and
puts everything back with Unsuppressed. Nothing is deleted. The
references can't be suppressed whole.

SetThickness.text:
SetThickness sets a shell's wall thickness in mm; SetExpr with
sketch.GroupPitch gives it an expression in the document's unit.

SetTurn.text:
SetTurn turns a loft's second profile by n curves, which joins its
curves to others of the first: a square lofted to a square turned by
one twists by a quarter.

SetVisible.text: SetVisible shows or hides the group.

Shell.text:
Shell is the exact surfaces of the model up to and with this group;
like Mesh, it is the sketch's own.

Solid.text: Solid is the solid at this group: the solid of every group up to it.

SolidEdges.text:
SolidEdges are the edges of the solid a chamfer cuts or a fillet
rounds by name.

Solved.text: Solved reports whether the solver satisfied the group's constraints.

String.text:
String describes the group as the property browser does:
"g003-extrude".

Suppression.text: Suppression is the group's suppress mode, as SetSuppress set it.

Thickness.text: Thickness is a shell's wall thickness in mm.

Triangles.text:
Triangles is how many triangles the model has up to and with this
group.

Turn.text:
Turn is how many curves a loft turns its second profile by before
joining curve by curve.

Type.text: Type is the group's type, as the sketch package names them.

UsedBy.text:
UsedBy lists the groups that refer to this group directly, in
history order.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the group exists.

Value.text:
Value is one of the group's values: the number of copies, the pitch
in mm, or the scale.

Visible.text: Visible reports whether the group is shown.

Volume.text: Volume is the volume in mm³ of the model up to and with this group.

Workplane.text: Workplane is the workplane of a group that is drawn in one.

Host.text:
Host owns a sketch on behalf of a Doc: it is the program around the
sketch, with or without windows. All of it but Run must be called
inside Run.

Param.text:
Param is one of the numbers the solver works out: a coordinate of a
point, a radius, the depth of an extrusion.

Set.text:
Set gives the parameter a value for the solver to start from; what
constrains it decides where it ends.

String.text: String shows the parameter's value.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the parameter exists.

Parameter.text:
Parameter is a named value of the document's parameter table, which
expressions on dimensions and group values can name, as Edit >
Parameters shows it. It is not a Param, which is one of the solver's
unknowns.

Request.text:
Request is something that was drawn: a line segment, a circle, a
datum point. The property browser lists the requests of a group.

Construction.text: Construction reports whether the request is construction geometry.

Delete.text: Delete deletes the request and the constraints on it.

Entity.text:
Entity is the entity the request makes: the line, the circle. Its
points are that entity's Points.

Group.text: Group is the group the request is in.

SetConstruction.text: SetConstruction makes the request construction geometry, or not.

String.text:
String describes the request as the property browser does:
"r004-line-segment".

Type.text: Type is the request's type, as the sketch package names them.

Valid.text: Valid reports whether the request exists.

Section.text:
Section is the state of the section view, as its screen shows it,
and the cut of the active group's solid.

SketchHost.text:
SketchHost is a Host for a bare sketch, with no user interface: what
Open and New make outside the application.

Activate.text: Activate makes a group the active one.

AddGroup.text:
AddGroup adds g after the active group, activates it, and
regenerates.

BeginEval.text:
BeginEval starts a step of a script: its first change is remembered
for undo.

Changing.text:
Changing remembers the sketch for undo before the first change of
a script's step.

DeleteGroup.text:
DeleteGroup deletes a group, activating the one before it if it was
active, and regenerates.

EndEval.text: EndEval ends a step of a script: what it changed is regenerated.

Export.decl: func (h *SketchHost) Export(kind ExportKind, path string) error
Export.text:
Export writes the mesh as STL; the other formats need the
application around the sketch.

Load.text: Load replaces the sketch by the one in a .spcs file.

MmPerUnit.text: MmPerUnit is 1: with no interface, lengths are shown in mm.

Redo.text:
Redo does again the last step undone, and reports whether there was
one.

Render.decl: func (h *SketchHost) Render(path string, _, _ int, _, _ geom.Vector) error
Render.text: Render fails: drawing needs the application around the sketch.

Run.text: Run runs fn at once: a bare sketch has no goroutine of its own.

RunCommand.text: RunCommand is an error: a sketch with no window has no menu.

Save.text:
Save writes the sketch to a .spcs file, its links made relative to
it.

Select.text: Select does nothing, for the same reason.

Selection.text: Selection is nothing: there is no interface to select in.

SetChordTolerance.text: SetChordTolerance sets the sketch's chord tolerance.

Undo.text: Undo takes back the last step, and reports whether there was one.

Solid.text:
Solid is the solid at a group, as its topology sees it: faces, the
edges where two faces meet, and the vertices where edges end. Its
edges have names that outlive a regeneration, so a script can keep
one and use it after changing the model upstream.

Edge.text:
Edge is the edge a name, as SolidEdge.Name writes it, names; it fails
when the name doesn't resolve, saying why.

EdgeAt.text:
EdgeAt is the edge nearest the point p, which must be within a
hundredth of a millimetre of it.

Edges.text:
Edges are the solid's edges that lie between two faces, in the
order the topology finds them.

EdgesAlong.text: EdgesAlong are the straight edges parallel to dir, either way.

EdgesBetween.text:
EdgesBetween are the edges where faces a and b meet, in the order
their names number them.

Euler.text:
Euler is the solid's Euler characteristic, V - E + F less the holes
in faces: 2 for a solid with no hole through it, 0 for one with one.
