RemapLatheEnd.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapLatheStart.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapLineToFace.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapPtToArc.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapPtToLine.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapPtToNormal.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

RemapTop.text: Remap keys for entity copies made by Group::Generate (C++ Group::REMAP_*).

github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/srf.name: srf
github.com/spacesolve/spacesolve/pkg/srf.text: Package srf mirrors the C++ srf/ module: NURBS/Bezier primitives, trimmed surfaces, watertight shells, BSP trees, and mesh boolean operations.

BspClass.text: BspClass is the side of a BSP node's plane something is on (C++ BspClass).

Class.text: Class is the relationship between a curve/edge and a face of the shell.

CurveSource.text: CurveSource tracks the provenance of a curve (used by SShell boolean operations to decide what to keep).

EarType.text: EarType classifies a vertex for ear-clipping triangulation.

EdgeKind.text: EdgeKind classifies edges emitted by SMesh::MakeOutlinesInto.

EdgeOnInfo.text: EdgeOnInfo is what FindEdgeOn learns about an edge (C++ SKdNode::EdgeOnInfo).

FaceFlag.text: FaceFlag controls mesh/shell rendering and CSG behavior.

FaceID.text: FaceID is a stable identifier for a face within a shell.

HalfSpace.text: HalfSpace is the points p with N.p <= D: what a section plane keeps, its normal N pointing to the side cut away.

Contains.text: Contains reports whether p is in the half space, or within LengthEps of its plane.

MeshMeta.text: MeshMeta is the colour/face tag attached to one triangle of an SMesh or to one surface of an SShell.

ParallelMode.text: ParallelMode says which loops of a Boolean run on several goroutines.

PolylineBuilder.text: PolylineBuilder assembles scattered edges into contiguous polylines (C++ PolylineBuilder, polyline.cpp).

AddEdge.decl: func (b *PolylineBuilder) AddEdge(p0, p1 geom.Vector, kind uint32) *PolylineEdge
AddEdge.text: AddEdge adds the edge p0-p1, unless it is degenerate or already there in the same direction (C++ PolylineBuilder::AddEdge).

AddVertex.text: AddVertex returns the vertex at pos, adding it if new (C++ PolylineBuilder::AddVertex).

Clear.text: Clear drops every vertex and edge (C++ PolylineBuilder::Clear).

Generate.decl: func (b *PolylineBuilder) Generate( startFn func(start, next *PolylineVertex, e *PolylineEdge), nextFn func(next *PolylineVertex, e *PolylineEdge), aloneFn func(e *PolylineEdge), endFn func(), )
Generate.text: Generate walks the edges as polylines: startFn for each polyline's first edge, nextFn for each following one, endFn after each polyline, and aloneFn for the edges left over (C++ PolylineBuilder::Generate).

GenerateEdges.text: GenerateEdges writes the polylines as edges (C++ PolylineBuilder::GenerateEdges).

GenerateOutlines.text: GenerateOutlines writes the polylines as outlines, each keeping its source outline's normals and tag (C++ PolylineBuilder::GenerateOutlines).

MakeFromEdges.text: MakeFromEdges adds sel's edges, with auxA as the kind (C++ PolylineBuilder::MakeFromEdges).

MakeFromOutlines.text: MakeFromOutlines adds the outlines, with the tag as the kind so that emphasized and contour outlines stay apart (C++ PolylineBuilder::MakeFromOutlines).

PolylineEdge.text: PolylineEdge is an edge between two vertices; Outline or Edge is the source it was made from (C++ PolylineBuilder::Edge).

OtherVertex.text: OtherVertex is the edge's end that isn't v (C++ Edge::GetOtherVertex).

PolylineVertex.text: PolylineVertex is a joint between edges (C++ PolylineBuilder::Vertex).

Rigid.text: Rigid is the rigid motion p -> Q p + T.

Then.text: Then is r followed by s.

SBezier.text: SBezier is a rational Bezier curve of degree 1..3 with up to 4 weighted 3-D control points.

AllIntersectionsWith.text: AllIntersectionsWith adds to spl the points where this curve crosses sbb: their pwls' crossings, refined onto both curves.

ClosestPointTo.decl: func (b *SBezier) ClosestPointTo(p geom.Vector, mustConverge bool) (float64, bool)
ClosestPointTo.text: ClosestPointTo is the parameter t of the point on the curve closest to p: the closest of a few samples, refined by Newton's method.

Equals.text: Equals returns true if two SBezier curves have identical degree, control points, and weights (within LENGTH_EPS tolerance).

Finish.text: Finish returns the last control point.

GetBoundingProjd.decl: func (b *SBezier) GetBoundingProjd(u, orig geom.Vector, pmin, pmax *float64)
GetBoundingProjd.text: GetBoundingProjd extends (pmin, pmax) with the projection of every control point onto the axis (orig + t * u).

InPerspective.decl: func (b *SBezier) InPerspective(u, v, n, origin geom.Vector, cameraTan float64) SBezier
InPerspective.text: InPerspective applies a perspective transformation, recomputing the rational weights.

IsCircle.decl: func (b *SBezier) IsCircle(axis geom.Vector, center *geom.Vector, r *float64) bool
IsCircle.text: IsCircle reports whether this curve is a circular arc about axis; if so its center and radius are returned.

IsInPlane.decl: func (b *SBezier) IsInPlane(n geom.Vector, d float64) bool
IsInPlane.text: IsInPlane reports whether every control point lies in the plane n .

IsRational.text: IsRational reports whether a weight differs from 1 (C++ SBezier::IsRational).

MakePwlInto.text: MakePwlInto emits the pwl approximation as edges.

MakePwlIntoContour.text: MakePwlIntoContour appends the pwl approximation to sc.

MakePwlIntoPoints.text: MakePwlIntoPoints splits the curve into piecewise linear segments that don't deviate from it by more than chordTol (0 means the default).

PointAt.text: PointAt evaluates the rational Bezier at parameter t.

PointOnNonparallelCurve.text: PointOnNonparallelCurve is like PointOnThisAndCurve but rejects parallel-curve configurations that would converge to a degenerate solution.

PointOnThisAndCurve.text: PointOnThisAndCurve finds a point that lies on both this bezier and the other bezier, by iteratively minimizing the closest distances.

Reverse.text: Reverse reverses the curve in place (reverses control points and weights).

ScaleSelfBy.text: ScaleSelfBy multiplies every control point by s.

SplitAt.text: SplitAt splits the curve at t into the part before and the part after, by de Casteljau's algorithm on the homogeneous control points (C++ SBezier::SplitAt).

Start.text: Start returns the first control point.

TangentAt.text: TangentAt is the derivative of the curve at t (C++ SBezier::TangentAt).

TransformedBy.decl: func (b *SBezier) TransformedBy(t geom.Vector, q geom.Quaternion, scale float64)
TransformedBy.text: TransformedBy applies (translation, rotation, scale) to every control point.

SBezierList.text: SBezierList is an ordered slice of SBezier curves.

AllIntersectionsWith.text: AllIntersectionsWith adds to spl the points where any curve of this list crosses any of other (C++ SBezierList::AllIntersectionsWith).

CullIdenticalBeziers.text: CullIdenticalBeziers removes the curves identical to an earlier one, either way round, and with both the earlier one too (C++ SBezierList::CullIdenticalBeziers).

GetBoundingProjd.decl: func (l *SBezierList) GetBoundingProjd(u, orig geom.Vector, pmin, pmax *float64)
GetBoundingProjd.text: GetBoundingProjd extends the box (min, max) to contain the projection of every control point onto the axis through orig in direction u.

GetPlaneContainingBeziers.decl: func (l *SBezierList) GetPlaneContainingBeziers(p, u, v *geom.Vector, notCoplanarAt *geom.Vector) bool
GetPlaneContainingBeziers.text: GetPlaneContainingBeziers finds a plane that contains all the curves in this list.

ScaleSelfBy.text: ScaleSelfBy multiplies every control point by s.

SBezierLoop.text: SBezierLoop is an ordered list of SBezier forming one closed (or open) loop.

GetBoundingProjd.decl: func (l *SBezierLoop) GetBoundingProjd(u, orig geom.Vector, pmin, pmax *float64)
GetBoundingProjd.text: GetBoundingProjd extends the axis-aligned bounding box.

IsClosed.text: IsClosed reports whether the loop ends where it starts (C++ SBezierLoop::IsClosed).

MakePwlInto.text: MakePwlInto emits the polyline approximation of this loop into el, with a chord tolerance of chordTol.

MakePwlIntoContour.text: MakePwlIntoContour appends the loop's pwl approximation to sc, without doubled points at the joins, and closes it exactly.

Reverse.text: Reverse reverses the loop order and every curve in it, so that each curve still starts where the previous one finishes.

SBezierLoopSet.text: SBezierLoopSet is a planar (closed) curve set: one outer contour plus zero or more hole contours.

GetBoundingProjd.decl: func (s *SBezierLoopSet) GetBoundingProjd(u, orig geom.Vector, pmin, pmax *float64)
GetBoundingProjd.text: GetBoundingProjd extends the axis-aligned bounding box from every contour in the set.

Loops.text: loops returns the set's loops in C++ order: the outer loop first, then the holes.

MakePwlInto.text: MakePwlInto adds one contour to sp for each loop, outer loop first (C++ SBezierLoopSet::MakePwlInto).

SignedArea.text: SignedArea is the set's area about its own normal, computed on first use (C++ SBezierLoopSet::SignedArea).

SBezierLoopSetSet.text: SBezierLoopSetSet is the top-level container for an entire sketch: a list of SBezierLoopSet (one per outer contour) plus an optional list of open paths.

AddOpenPath.text: AddOpenPath adds a set holding a loop of just b (C++ SBezierLoopSetSet::AddOpenPath).

AddOuter.text: AddOuter appends a new empty SBezierLoopSet and returns a pointer to it.

FindOuterFacesFrom.decl: func (s *SBezierLoopSetSet) FindOuterFacesFrom(sbl *SBezierList, spxyz *SPolygon, srfuv *SSurface, chordTol float64, allClosed *bool, notClosedAt *SEdge, allCoplanar *bool, notCoplanarAt *geom.Vector, openContours *[]SBezierLoop)
FindOuterFacesFrom.text: FindOuterFacesFrom assembles the curves of sbl into closed loops and groups each outer loop with its holes into one SBezierLoopSet.

SBsp2.text: SBsp2 is a 2d BSP over the edges of the triangles in a 3d node's plane: the line through edge, in the plane with normal np, with outward normal no, at no .

InsertEdge.text: InsertEdge inserts nedge below this node, splitting it against the node's line (C++ SBsp2::InsertEdge).

InsertTriangle.text: InsertTriangle classifies tr, which lies in the 3d node's plane, against the edges in that plane, splitting it as needed (C++ SBsp2::InsertTriangle).

InsertTriangleHow.decl: func (b *SBsp2) InsertTriangleHow(how BspClass, tr *STriangle, m *SMesh, bsp3 *SBsp3)
InsertTriangleHow.text: InsertTriangleHow passes tr down the given side, or, where the tree ends, decides it against the 3d node's plane (C++ SBsp2::InsertTriangleHow).

IntersectionWith.text: IntersectionWith is where the segment from a to b, which must cross the node's line, crosses it (C++ SBsp2::IntersectionWith).

SBsp3.text: SBsp3 is a node of a 3d BSP: the plane n .

GenerateInPaintOrder.text: GenerateInPaintOrder lists the tree's triangles back to front along z (C++ SBsp3::GenerateInPaintOrder).

Insert.text: Insert inserts tr below this node, splitting it against the node's plane (C++ SBsp3::Insert).

InsertConvex.text: InsertConvex inserts a convex polygon, splitting it against the node's plane as a polygon where it can (C++ SBsp3::InsertConvex).

InsertConvexHow.decl: func (b *SBsp3) InsertConvexHow(how BspClass, meta STriMeta, vertex []geom.Vector, instead *SMesh)
InsertConvexHow.text: InsertConvexHow inserts a convex polygon on the given side of the node (C++ SBsp3::InsertConvexHow).

InsertHow.text: InsertHow inserts tr on the given side of the node, or, when instead is set and the tree ends there, decides whether the Boolean keeps it (C++ SBsp3::InsertHow).

InsertInPlane.text: InsertInPlane adds tr, which lies in the node's plane, to m if the Boolean keeps it: by whether a triangle in the plane covers its centroid, and on which side (C++ SBsp3::InsertInPlane).

IntersectionWith.text: IntersectionWith is where the segment from a to b, which must cross the node's plane, crosses it (C++ SBsp3::IntersectionWith).

SBspUv.text: SBspUv is a 2-D BSP tree over uv-space edges, used to test whether a point (u, v) on a surface lies inside or outside the trim region.

ClassifyEdge.decl: func (b *SBspUv) ClassifyEdge(ea, eb geom.Point2d, srf *SSurface) BspUvClass
ClassifyEdge.text: ClassifyEdge classifies the edge ea->eb by its midpoint, retrying at another point if the midpoint lands on a non-parallel trim edge.

ClassifyPoint.decl: func (b *SBspUv) ClassifyPoint(p, eb geom.Point2d, srf *SSurface) BspUvClass
ClassifyPoint.text: ClassifyPoint classifies p against the trim region.

MinimumDistanceToEdge.text: MinimumDistanceToEdge returns the xyz-scaled distance from p to the nearest trim edge.

SContour.text: SContour is an ordered list of SPoint forming one polygon contour.

AddPoint.text: AddPoint appends p with tag 0 (C++ SContour::AddPoint).

AnyEdgeMidpoint.text: AnyEdgeMidpoint returns the midpoint of the first edge.

BridgeToContour.text: BridgeToContour merges the hole sc into this (open, i.e.

ClipEarInto.decl: func (c *SContour) ClipEarInto(m *SMesh, bp int, scaledEps float64)
ClipEarInto.text: ClipEarInto adds the triangle at vertex bp to m (unless degenerate) and removes that vertex.

ComputeNormal.text: ComputeNormal returns the unit face normal of the contour's plane (best-fit for non-planar contours).

CopyInto.text: CopyInto adds the contour's points to dest (C++ SContour::CopyInto).

FindPointWithMinX.text: FindPointWithMinX sets XMinPt to the first point with the least x (C++ SContour::FindPointWithMinX).

IsClockwiseProjdToNormal.text: IsClockwiseProjdToNormal mirrors C++ SContour::IsClockwiseProjdToNormal (polygon.cpp:603), including its sign convention (see SignedAreaProjdToNormal).

IsEar.decl: func (c *SContour) IsEar(bp int, scaledEps float64) bool
IsEar.text: IsEar reports whether vertex bp can be clipped.

IsEmptyTriangle.decl: func (c *SContour) IsEmptyTriangle(ap, bp, cp int, scaledEPS float64) bool
IsEmptyTriangle.text: IsEmptyTriangle reports whether no other point of the contour lies in the triangle (ap, bp, cp).

MakeEdgesInto.text: MakeEdgesInto adds an edge for each pair of consecutive points; the contour repeats its first point at the end, so it is closed (C++ SContour::MakeEdgesInto).

OffsetInto.text: OffsetInto adds to dest the contour, in the xy plane, offset by r: outside corners are rounded, inside ones mitred (C++ SContour::OffsetInto).

Reverse.text: Reverse reverses the contour direction in place.

UvTriangulateInto.text: UvTriangulateInto ear-clips this single (hole-free) uv contour into m.

SCurve.text: SCurve is a trim curve in the shell: the exact SBezier form plus the polyline approximation, and references to the two surfaces it trims.

GetAxisAlignedBounding.text: GetAxisAlignedBounding computes the xyz bounding box of this SCurve's exact Bezier.

GetSurfaceA.text: GetSurfaceA returns the surface named by SurfA, looked up in the operand the curve came from.

GetSurfaceB.text: GetSurfaceB returns the surface named by SurfB, looked up in the operand the curve came from.

MakeCopySplitAgainst.decl: func (c *SCurve) MakeCopySplitAgainst(agnstA, agnstB *SShell, srfA, srfB *SSurface) SCurve
MakeCopySplitAgainst.text: MakeCopySplitAgainst returns a copy of c whose pwl is split wherever it crosses a (trimmed, or nearly trimmed) surface of agnstA or agnstB, and at any trim vertex of those shells lying on the curve.

RemoveShortSegments.text: RemoveShortSegments drops the polyline points that aren't vertices, aren't spaced deliberately along an exact curve, and aren't needed to meet the chord tolerance in either surface.

RemoveShortSegmentsWithChordTol.text: RemoveShortSegmentsWithChordTol is RemoveShortSegments with an explicit chord tolerance in place of ChordTolMm().

SCurvePt.text: SCurvePt is one polyline vertex on a trim curve.

SEdge.text: SEdge is a 3-D line segment used by SEdgeList for polygon assembly and kd-tree queries.

Crossing.decl: func (e *SEdge) Crossing(p0, dp geom.Vector) (t float64, ok bool)
Crossing.text: Crossing reports the parametric t along edge e at which line (p0, dp) crosses e.

EdgeCrosses.decl: func (e *SEdge) EdgeCrosses(ea, eb geom.Vector, ppi *geom.Vector, spl *SPointList) bool
EdgeCrosses.text: EdgeCrosses reports whether the segment ea->eb crosses this edge.

SEdgeList.text: SEdgeList is a slice of SEdge.

AddEdge.decl: func (el *SEdgeList) AddEdge(a, b geom.Vector, auxA, auxB, tag int)

AnyEdgeCrossings.decl: func (el *SEdgeList) AnyEdgeCrossings(a, b geom.Vector, ppi *geom.Vector, spl *SPointList) int
AnyEdgeCrossings.text: AnyEdgeCrossings counts the edges that ea->eb crosses.

AssembleContour.decl: func (el *SEdgeList) AssembleContour(first, last geom.Vector, dest *SContour, errorAt *SEdge, keepDir bool, start int) bool
AssembleContour.text: AssembleContour chains untagged edges onto first->last until the contour closes.

AssemblePolygon.decl: func (el *SEdgeList) AssemblePolygon(dest *SPolygon, errorAt *SEdge, keepDir bool) bool
AssemblePolygon.text: AssemblePolygon assembles the edges into closed contours, using and setting each edge's Tag to mark it as consumed.

ContainsEdge.text: ContainsEdge reports whether el contains set, in either direction.

ContainsEdgeFrom.text: ContainsEdgeFrom reports whether any edge of el is also in sel (in either direction).

CullExtraneousEdges.text: CullExtraneousEdges removes duplicate edges, and anti-parallel pairs (both of them if both, else one).

MergeCollinearSegments.text: MergeCollinearSegments sorts the edges, which all lie on the line from a to b, along it, and merges each run of joined edges of the same style into one (C++ SEdgeList::MergeCollinearSegments).

SEdgeLl.text: SEdgeLl is a singly-linked list of edges, the payload of an SKdNodeEdges leaf (C++ SEdgeLl).

SInter.text: SInter is a ray-shell intersection point with metadata about the surfaces and curves it crossed.

SKdNode.text: SKdNode is a node of the kd-tree: an interior node splits space at coordinate Which == C, a leaf holds a list of triangles (C++ SKdNode).

AddTriangle.text: AddTriangle adds tr to every leaf whose region it touches.

ClearTags.text: ClearTags zeroes the tags of every triangle in the tree.

FindEdgeOn.decl: func (n *SKdNode) FindEdgeOn(a, b geom.Vector, cnt int, coplanarIsInter bool, info *EdgeOnInfo)
FindEdgeOn.text: FindEdgeOn looks for triangles that are mates of the edge a -> b (an edge b -> a of theirs), counting them in info.Count; it also reports whether the edge crosses the mesh.

ListTrianglesInto.text: ListTrianglesInto lists each triangle of the tree once.

MakeCertainEdgesInto.decl: func (n *SKdNode) MakeCertainEdgesInto(sel *SEdgeList, how EdgeKind, coplanarIsInter bool, inter, leaky *bool, auxA int)
MakeCertainEdgesInto.text: MakeCertainEdgesInto picks certain classes of edges out from the mesh: naked edges (with no anti-parallel mate) and self-intersecting edges, or turning, emphasized or sharp edges.

MakeMeshInto.text: MakeMeshInto adds each triangle of the tree to m once.

MakeOutlinesInto.text: MakeOutlinesInto lists the edges shared by two triangles, tagged 1 where they are emphasized or sharp (per edgeKind); untagged edges between triangles with the same normal are left out (C++ SKdNode::MakeOutlinesInto).

OcclusionTestLine.decl: func (n *SKdNode) OcclusionTestLine(orig SEdge, sel *SEdgeList, cnt int)
OcclusionTestLine.text: OcclusionTestLine splits orig against the mesh into sel, tagging the hidden pieces (C++ SKdNode::OcclusionTestLine).

SnapToMesh.text: SnapToMesh snaps the tree to each vertex of each triangle of m; if m is the mesh the tree was made from, the result is vertex-to-vertex (C++ SKdNode::SnapToMesh).

SnapToVertex.text: SnapToVertex splits every triangle with an edge that goes through v (but not a vertex at v) so that it has a vertex there: the triangle is modified, and the new one goes in extras (C++ SKdNode::SnapToVertex).

SplitLinesAgainstTriangle.text: SplitLinesAgainstTriangle splits the edges of sel against tr, and tags those that tr hides when looking down z (C++ SKdNode::SplitLinesAgainstTriangle).

SKdNodeEdges.text: SKdNodeEdges is a kd-tree over edges, so that a query for the edges crossing one need only test those near it (C++ SKdNodeEdges).

AnyEdgeCrossings.decl: func (n *SKdNodeEdges) AnyEdgeCrossings(a, b geom.Vector, cnt int, pi *geom.Vector, spl *SPointList) int
AnyEdgeCrossings.text: AnyEdgeCrossings counts the edges of the tree that the edge from a to b crosses, as SEdge.EdgeCrosses decides, tagging each tested edge with cnt so that one on both sides of a split counts once; an edge already tagged cnt isn't tested (C++ SKdNodeEdges::AnyEdgeCrossings).

SMesh.text: SMesh is a list of triangles, with the flags the Booleans use to pick which triangles to keep (C++ SMesh).

AddAgainstBsp.text: AddAgainstBsp adds the triangles of srcm that the Boolean keeps against bsp3, as the mesh's flags say, split where they cross the other mesh (C++ SMesh::AddAgainstBsp).

AddTriangle.text: AddTriangle adds a copy of t (C++ SMesh::AddTriangle(const STriangle *)).

AddTriangle3.decl: func (m *SMesh) AddTriangle3(meta STriMeta, a, b, c geom.Vector)
AddTriangle3.text: AddTriangle3 adds the triangle a, b, c (C++ SMesh::AddTriangle(meta, a, b, c)).

AddTriangleN.decl: func (m *SMesh) AddTriangleN(meta STriMeta, n, a, b, c geom.Vector)
AddTriangleN.text: AddTriangleN adds the triangle a, b, c, wound so its normal points along n; a (nearly) collinear one is dropped (C++ SMesh::AddTriangle(meta, n, a, b, c)).

CalculateSurfaceArea.text: CalculateSurfaceArea is the area of the triangles on the given faces (C++ SMesh::CalculateSurfaceArea).

CalculateVolume.text: CalculateVolume is the volume the mesh encloses, integrated under each triangle (C++ SMesh::CalculateVolume).

Clear.text: Clear drops the triangles; like C++ SMesh::Clear it keeps the flags.

FirstIntersectionIn.decl: func (m *SMesh) FirstIntersectionIn(rayPoint, rayDir geom.Vector, h *HalfSpace) uint32
FirstIntersectionIn.text: FirstIntersectionIn is FirstIntersectionWith counting only hits in the half space h, if it isn't nil: a face cut away by a section isn't there to hit.

FirstIntersectionWith.text: FirstIntersectionWith is the face of the farthest-along triangle, with a face, that the ray rayPoint + t*rayDir hits; 0 if none.

GetBounding.text: GetBounding is the mesh's bounding box (C++ SMesh::GetBounding).

GetCenterOfMass.text: GetCenterOfMass is the centroid of the volume the mesh encloses (C++ SMesh::GetCenterOfMass).

MakeEdgesInPlaneInto.decl: func (m *SMesh) MakeEdgesInPlaneInto(sel *SEdgeList, n geom.Vector, d float64)
MakeEdgesInPlaneInto.text: MakeEdgesInPlaneInto reports the edges of the boundary of the region(s) of the mesh that lie within the plane n .

MakeFromAssemblyOf.text: MakeFromAssemblyOf adds the triangles of a and of b (C++ SMesh::MakeFromAssemblyOf).

MakeFromDifferenceOf.text: MakeFromDifferenceOf adds a minus b (C++ SMesh::MakeFromDifferenceOf).

MakeFromIntersectionOf.text: MakeFromIntersectionOf adds the intersection of a and b (C++ SMesh::MakeFromIntersectionOf).

MakeFromTransformationOf.decl: func (m *SMesh) MakeFromTransformationOf(a *SMesh, trans geom.Vector, q geom.Quaternion, scale float64)
MakeFromTransformationOf.text: MakeFromTransformationOf adds a's triangles, scaled, then rotated, then translated; a mirroring scale keeps the mesh outside out (C++ SMesh::MakeFromTransformationOf).

MakeFromUnionOf.text: MakeFromUnionOf adds the union of a and b (C++ SMesh::MakeFromUnionOf).

MakeOutlinesInto.text: MakeOutlinesInto lists the mesh's outline edges of the given kind (C++ SMesh::MakeOutlinesInto).

MakeSectionPolygonInto.text: MakeSectionPolygonInto puts the section of the mesh by the plane of h into dest: the loops where the plane cuts the triangles, to fill as the cap of a section view with the odd winding rule.

PrecomputeTransparency.text: PrecomputeTransparency sorts the opaque triangles before the transparent ones, for drawing, in std::sort's order; and notes whether the comparisons met a transparent triangle (C++ SMesh::PrecomputeTransparency).

RemapFaces.text: RemapFaces rewrites each triangle's face to the group's copy copyNumber of it (C++ SMesh::RemapFaces).

RemoveDegenerateTriangles.text: RemoveDegenerateTriangles drops the degenerate triangles (C++ SMesh::RemoveDegenerateTriangles).

Simplify.text: Simplify replaces the triangles from start on, which must be coplanar, with fewer ones covering the same area: it pastes them together into convex polygons, merging collinear edges where it can, and triangulates those.

WindingNumber.text: WindingNumber is how many times the mesh wraps around p: the sum of the solid angles its triangles subtend at p, over 4π (the formula of Van Oosterom and Strackee).

SOutline.text: SOutline is an edge between two triangles of a mesh, with the normals on its left and right (C++ SOutline).

IsVisible.text: IsVisible reports whether the edge is an outline when looking along projDir: one of its faces is toward the viewer and the other away (C++ SOutline::IsVisible).

SOutlineList.text: SOutlineList is a list of outline edges (C++ SOutlineList).

AddEdge.decl: func (l *SOutlineList) AddEdge(a, b, nl, nr geom.Vector, tag int)
AddEdge.text: AddEdge adds an outline edge (C++ SOutlineList::AddEdge).

ListTaggedInto.text: ListTaggedInto adds the tagged outline edges to el (C++ SOutlineList::ListTaggedInto).

MakeFromCopyOf.text: MakeFromCopyOf adds sol's outline edges (C++ SOutlineList::MakeFromCopyOf).

SPoint.text: SPoint is a single vertex on a planar polygon.

SPointList.text: SPointList is an ordered list of points, each with a tag (C++ SPointList).

Add.text: Add appends pt with tag 0 (C++ SPointList::Add).

ContainsPoint.text: ContainsPoint reports whether pt is one of the list's points (C++ SPointList::ContainsPoint).

IncrementTagFor.text: IncrementTagFor counts pt: it increments the tag of the point equal to pt, or adds pt with tag 1 (C++ SPointList::IncrementTagFor).

IndexForPoint.text: IndexForPoint is the index of the list's point equal to pt, or -1 (C++ SPointList::IndexForPoint).

SPolygon.text: SPolygon is a set of SContour on a common plane.

AnyPoint.text: AnyPoint returns a representative point (the first point of the first non-empty contour).

ComputeNormal.text: ComputeNormal is the first contour's normal (C++ SPolygon::ComputeNormal).

ContainsPoint.text: ContainsPoint mirrors C++ SPolygon::ContainsPoint (odd winding number about p.Normal).

FixContourDirections.text: FixContourDirections orients every contour so that outer contours look counterclockwise projected against p.Normal (in the C++ sense of IsClockwiseProjdToNormal) and holes the opposite way.

InverseTransformInto.decl: func (p *SPolygon) InverseTransformInto(sp *SPolygon, u, v, n geom.Vector)
InverseTransformInto.text: InverseTransformInto expresses every vertex in the (u, v, n) basis.

MakeEdgesInto.text: MakeEdgesInto emits one SEdge per consecutive pair of points in every contour, with closeLoop = true.

OffsetInto.text: OffsetInto sets dest to the polygon offset by r, contour by contour (C++ SPolygon::OffsetInto).

SelfIntersecting.text: SelfIntersecting reports whether any edge of the polygon crosses another, leaving a crossing in intersectsAt when it is given (C++ SPolygon::SelfIntersecting).

SignedArea.text: SignedArea is the polygon's area about its normal: the true area only if the contours are all oriented correctly, with the holes backwards from the outer contours (C++ SPolygon::SignedArea).

TriangulateInto.text: TriangulateInto triangulates this planar xyz polygon into m.

UvGridTriangulateInto.text: UvGridTriangulateInto covers the interior of the uv polygon with an adaptive grid of quads, cuts those out of the polygon, and ear-clips the rest.

UvTriangulateInto.text: UvTriangulateInto triangulates the uv-space polygon (contours stored closed, holes oriented opposite to outer contours) and adds the triangles, still in uv, to m.

SShell.text: SShell is a watertight collection of trimmed surfaces and the trim curves joining them.

AllPointsIntersecting.decl: func (s *SShell) AllPointsIntersecting(a, b geom.Vector, inters *[]SInter, asSegment, trimmed, inclTangent bool)
AllPointsIntersecting.text: AllPointsIntersecting collects the intersections of the line (a, b) with every surface of the shell.

ClassifyEdge.decl: func (s *SShell) ClassifyEdge(indir, outdir *Class, ea, eb, p, edgeNIn, edgeNOut, surfN geom.Vector) bool
ClassifyEdge.text: ClassifyEdge decides whether an edge (ea, eb) of a shell lies inside, outside, or coincident with the shell, in two directions (indir / outdir).

ClassifyRegion.decl: func (s *SShell) ClassifyRegion(edgeN, interSurfN, edgeSurfN geom.Vector) Class
ClassifyRegion.text: ClassifyRegion decides whether an edge lies inside or outside the shell at a point of contact, based on the relationship between three normals: the edge's normal, the intersecting surface's normal, and the shell's face normal at that point.

CleanupAfterBoolean.text: CleanupAfterBoolean clears the edges MakeClassifyingBsps made as a calculation aid (C++ SShell::CleanupAfterBoolean).

CopyCurvesSplitAgainst.text: CopyCurvesSplitAgainst copies every curve of s into `into`, split so that a pwl segment never crosses a surface of agnst, and records each original curve's handle in `into` as its NewH (for rewriting the trims).

CopySurfacesTrimAgainst.decl: func (s *SShell) CopySurfacesTrimAgainst(sha, shb, into *SShell, op SurfaceCombineAs)
CopySurfacesTrimAgainst.text: CopySurfacesTrimAgainst copies every surface of s into `into`, trimmed against the other operand per the boolean op, and records each surface's handle in `into` as its NewH. Mirrors C++ SShell::CopySurfacesTrimAgainst (boolean.cpp:750).

FindCurve.text: FindCurve returns the SCurve with the given handle, or nil if not found.

FindCurveBySurface.text: FindCurveBySurface returns all curves that reference the given surface as either SurfA or SurfB.

FindSurface.text: FindSurface returns the SSurface with the given handle, or nil if not found.

MakeClassifyingBsps.text: MakeClassifyingBsps pre-computes uv-space BSPs for every surface in the shell.

MakeCoincidentEdgesInto.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeCoincidentEdgesInto(proto *SSurface, sameNormal bool, el *SEdgeList, useCurvesFrom *SShell)
MakeCoincidentEdgesInto.text: MakeCoincidentEdgesInto copies into el the trim polygons of every surface in the shell that is coincident with proto (with the same or opposite normal, as asked), in proto's uv coordinates (C++ SShell::MakeCoincidentEdgesInto).

MakeEdgesInto.text: MakeEdgesInto extracts the trim edges of every surface as SEdge entries.

MakeFirstOrderRevolvedSurfaces.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFirstOrderRevolvedSurfaces(pt, axis geom.Vector, i0 int)
MakeFirstOrderRevolvedSurfaces.text: MakeFirstOrderRevolvedSurfaces rewrites the surfaces from index i0 on that are revolutions of a line into lower-order forms where possible: a revolution in a plane perpendicular to the axis becomes a degree (1, 1) plane, and a cylinder is transposed so that it is recognized as a surface of extrusion.

MakeFromAssemblyOf.text: MakeFromAssemblyOf copies all the surfaces and curves from two different shells into a single shell, rewriting their handles; it doesn't look for any surface intersections, so if two objects interfere then the result is just self-intersecting.

MakeFromBoolean.text: MakeFromBoolean sets s to the boolean combination of a and b.

MakeFromCopyOf.text: MakeFromCopyOf copies src (C++ SShell::MakeFromCopyOf): a transformation by the identity, which, like C++'s, still rotates and translates the curves' exact forms (so turns -0 into +0).

MakeFromExtrusionOf.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFromExtrusionOf(sbls *SBezierLoopSet, t0, t1 geom.Vector, color core.RgbaColor)
MakeFromExtrusionOf.text: MakeFromExtrusionOf extrudes a planar BezierLoopSet from t0 to t1.

MakeFromHelicalRevolutionOf.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFromHelicalRevolutionOf(sbls *SBezierLoopSet, pt, axis geom.Vector, color core.RgbaColor, group ShellGroup, angles, anglef, dists, distf float64)
MakeFromHelicalRevolutionOf.text: MakeFromHelicalRevolutionOf sweeps a planar BezierLoopSet around the axis (pt, axis) from angle angles to anglef while translating along the axis from dists to distf.

MakeFromRevolutionOf.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFromRevolutionOf(sbls *SBezierLoopSet, pt, axis geom.Vector, color core.RgbaColor, group ShellGroup)
MakeFromRevolutionOf.text: MakeFromRevolutionOf revolves a planar BezierLoopSet a full turn around the axis (pt, axis).

MakeFromSweepOf.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFromSweepOf(sbls *SBezierLoopSet, steps []SweepStep, color core.RgbaColor, startFace, endFace FaceID)
MakeFromSweepOf.text: MakeFromSweepOf adds the solid the planar loop set sbls sweeps through as it moves along steps, a chain whose pieces meet tangent: one side surface per curve and piece, an extrusion for a straight piece and a surface of revolution for each quarter of a turn, and a cap at each end, startFace at the profile and endFace where the steps take it.

MakeFromTransformationOf.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeFromTransformationOf(a *SShell, t geom.Vector, q geom.Quaternion, scale float64)
MakeFromTransformationOf.text: MakeFromTransformationOf applies (translate, rotate, scale) to every surface and curve of src, keeping their original handles.

MakeIntersectionCurvesAgainst.text: MakeIntersectionCurvesAgainst computes the surface-surface intersection curves between every pair of surfaces (one from `s`, one from `agnst`) and appends them to into.Curve.

MakePrism.decl: func (s *SShell) MakePrism(pts []geom.Vector, t0, t1 geom.Vector, color core.RgbaColor)
MakePrism.text: MakePrism adds the prism of the plane polygon pts swept from t0 to t1, which must not lie in the polygon's plane.

MakeSectionEdgesInto.decl: func (s *SShell) MakeSectionEdgesInto(n geom.Vector, d float64, sel *SEdgeList, sbl *SBezierList)
MakeSectionEdgesInto.text: MakeSectionEdgesInto reports the trim curves of the shell's planar faces that lie in the plane n .

MergeCoincidentSurfaces.text: MergeCoincidentSurfaces merges coincident, same-color planes that share an edge into one surface carrying all of their trims.

RemapFaces.text: RemapFaces rewrites each surface's face to the group's copy copyNumber of it (C++ SShell::RemapFaces).

RewriteSurfaceHandlesForCurves.text: RewriteSurfaceHandlesForCurves points every curve's SurfA/SurfB at the new handles of its surfaces in s.

TriangulateInto.text: TriangulateInto triangulates every surface in the shell and appends the resulting triangles to mesh.

SShellClass.text: SShellClass mirrors the C++ SShell::Class enum (srf/surface.h:420).

SSurface.text: SSurface is a rational Bezier surface patch in (u, v).

AddExactIntersectionCurve.decl: func (s *SSurface) AddExactIntersectionCurve(sb *SBezier, srfB *SSurface, agnstA, agnstB *SShell, into *SShell)
AddExactIntersectionCurve.text: AddExactIntersectionCurve adds the exact curve sb, where s meets srfB, to into: its pwl follows an identical curve already in into, or else is split against the operand shells (C++ SSurface::AddExactIntersectionCurve).

AllPointsIntersecting.decl: func (s *SSurface) AllPointsIntersecting(a, b geom.Vector, l *[]SInter, asSegment, trimmed, inclTangent bool)
AllPointsIntersecting.text: AllPointsIntersecting finds all points where the line through a and b intersects this surface and appends them to l.

AllPointsIntersectingUntrimmed.decl: func (s *SSurface) AllPointsIntersectingUntrimmed(a, b geom.Vector, cnt, level *int, l *[]surfInter, asSegment bool, sorig *SSurface)
AllPointsIntersectingUntrimmed.text: AllPointsIntersectingUntrimmed recursively subdivides the surface until each piece is nearly flat, then refines with Newton.

BlendRowOrCol.decl: func (s *SSurface) BlendRowOrCol(row bool, thisIJ int, a *SSurface, aIJ int, b *SSurface, bIJ int)
BlendRowOrCol.text: BlendRowOrCol sets row (or column) thisIJ to the average of row aIJ of a and row bIJ of b (C++ SSurface::BlendRowOrCol).

ChordToleranceForEdge.text: ChordToleranceForEdge returns how far the surface deviates from the straight xyz segment between the uv points a and b.

ClosestPointOnThisAndSurface.text: ClosestPointOnThisAndSurface returns the point on the intersection of s and srf2 closest to p.

ClosestPointTo.decl: func (s *SSurface) ClosestPointTo(p geom.Vector, puv *geom.Point2d, mustConverge bool)
ClosestPointTo.text: ClosestPointTo finds the (u, v) of the point on the surface closest to p (C++ SSurface::ClosestPointTo).

ClosestPointToUV.decl: func (s *SSurface) ClosestPointToUV(p geom.Vector, u, v *float64, mustConverge bool)
ClosestPointToUV.text: ClosestPointToUV is ClosestPointTo returning u and v separately.

CoincidentWith.text: CoincidentWith reports whether ss is a plane lying in the same plane as s, with the same (or, if !sameNormal, opposite) normal.

CoincidentWithPlane.decl: func (s *SSurface) CoincidentWithPlane(n geom.Vector, d float64) bool
CoincidentWithPlane.text: CoincidentWithPlane reports whether the surface is a plane lying in the plane n .

ContainsPlaneCurve.text: ContainsPlaneCurve returns true if the supplied exact curve lies entirely within the plane of this surface.

CopyRowOrCol.decl: func (s *SSurface) CopyRowOrCol(row bool, thisIJ int, src *SSurface, srcIJ int)
CopyRowOrCol.text: CopyRowOrCol copies row (or column) srcIJ of src into row thisIJ (C++ SSurface::CopyRowOrCol).

DepartureFromCoplanar.text: DepartureFromCoplanar is how far the control points stray from the plane through three of them, chosen far apart (C++ SSurface::DepartureFromCoplanar).

EdgeCurveIntersection.text: EdgeCurveIntersection is a fallback for PointIntersectingLine: tries to intersect the line with the boundary curve of the surface.

ExactSurfaceTangentAt.decl: func (srf *SSurface) ExactSurfaceTangentAt(p geom.Vector, srfA, srfB *SSurface, dir geom.Vector) geom.Vector
ExactSurfaceTangentAt.text: ExactSurfaceTangentAt is the direction, at p, of the curve where srfA meets srfB, pointing along dir (C++ SSurface::ExactSurfaceTangentAt).

GetAxisAlignedBounding.text: GetAxisAlignedBounding extends (ptMin, ptMax) to include every control point of the surface.

IntersectAgainst.text: IntersectAgainst adds the curves where s meets b to into (C++ SSurface::IntersectAgainst).

IsCylinder.decl: func (s *SSurface) IsCylinder(axis, center *geom.Vector, r *float64, start, finish *geom.Vector) bool
IsCylinder.text: IsCylinder reports whether this surface is an extruded circular arc.

IsExtrusion.text: IsExtrusion reports whether this surface is an extrusion; if so and of is non-nil, the extruded curve and direction are returned.

LineEntirelyOutsideBbox.decl: func (s *SSurface) LineEntirelyOutsideBbox(a, b geom.Vector, asSegment bool) bool
LineEntirelyOutsideBbox.text: LineEntirelyOutsideBbox returns true if the line (a, b) does not cross the surface's bounding box.

MakeEdgesInto.decl: func (srf *SSurface) MakeEdgesInto(shell *SShell, sel *SEdgeList, asUV bool, useCurvesFrom *SShell)
MakeEdgesInto.text: MakeEdgesInto emits the pwl edges of every trim curve of srf, in uv space (asUV) or xyz.

MakeTriangulationGridInto.decl: func (s *SSurface) MakeTriangulationGridInto(l *[]float64, vs, vf float64, swapped bool, depth int)
MakeTriangulationGridInto.text: MakeTriangulationGridInto appends grid lines in (vs, vf] spaced to satisfy the chord tolerance.

NormalAt.text: NormalAt returns the (unnormalized) surface normal at (u, v), the cross product of the tangents (C++ SSurface::NormalAt).

NormalAtMaybeSwapped.decl: func (s *SSurface) NormalAtMaybeSwapped(u, v float64, swapped bool) geom.Vector

PointAt.text: PointAt evaluates the surface at parameter (u, v).

PointAtMaybeSwapped.decl: func (s *SSurface) PointAtMaybeSwapped(u, v float64, swapped bool) geom.Vector

PointIntersectingLine.decl: func (s *SSurface) PointIntersectingLine(p0, p1 geom.Vector, u, v *float64) bool
PointIntersectingLine.text: PointIntersectingLine refines (u, v) by Newton's method to where the line through p0 and p1 meets the surface, trying the surface's edge if that fails (C++ SSurface::PointIntersectingLine).

PointOnCurve.text: PointOnCurve refines (*up, *vp), an initial guess, to where curve pierces the surface, by alternating Newton iterations: each finds where the curve's tangent line pierces the surface's tangent plane, then updates both the surface (u, v) and the curve parameter.

PointOnSurfaces.text: PointOnSurfaces refines (*up, *vp) on s so that the point also lies on s1 and s2.

Reverse.text: Reverse flips the first parameter direction, which flips the normal, and reverses the trims to match.

ScaleSelfBy.text: ScaleSelfBy multiplies every control point by s.

SplitInHalf.text: SplitInHalf splits the surface at u = 0.5 (byU) or v = 0.5 into sa and sb, by de Casteljau's algorithm in projective space (C++ SSurface::SplitInHalf).

TangentsAt.decl: func (s *SSurface) TangentsAt(u, v float64, tu, tv *geom.Vector, retry bool)
TangentsAt.text: TangentsAt computes the partial derivatives dP/du and dP/dv at (u, v) (C++ SSurface::TangentsAt).

UnWeightControlPoints.text: UnWeightControlPoints divides each control point by its weight (C++ SSurface::UnWeightControlPoints).

WeightControlPoints.text: WeightControlPoints multiplies each control point by its weight (C++ SSurface::WeightControlPoints).

STriMeta.text: STriMeta is the colour/face tag attached to each STriangle.

STriangle.text: STriangle is one face of an SMesh.

Area.text: Area is the triangle's area (C++ STriangle::Area).

ContainsPoint.text: ContainsPoint reports whether p, projected along the normal, lies in the triangle; never for a zero-area triangle (C++ STriangle::ContainsPoint).

ContainsPointProjd.text: ContainsPointProjd reports whether p, projected along n, lies in the triangle (edges included; C++ STriangle::ContainsPointProjd).

FlipNormal.text: FlipNormal swaps a and b (C++ STriangle::FlipNormal).

IsDegenerate.text: IsDegenerate reports whether a vertex lies on the opposite edge (C++ STriangle::IsDegenerate).

MinAltitude.text: MinAltitude is the triangle's smallest altitude (C++ STriangle::MinAltitude).

Normal.text: Normal is the triangle's unnormalized normal (C++ STriangle::Normal).

Raytrace.decl: func (t *STriangle) Raytrace(rayPoint, rayDir geom.Vector) (tt float64, inters geom.Vector, ok bool)
Raytrace.text: Raytrace intersects the ray rayPoint + t*rayDir with the triangle, which must face against the ray (C++ STriangle::Raytrace; the Moeller-Trumbore algorithm).

SignedVolume.text: SignedVolume is the signed volume of the tetrahedron of the triangle and the origin (C++ STriangle::SignedVolume).

Transform.decl: func (t STriangle) Transform(u, v, n geom.Vector) STriangle
Transform.text: Transform takes every vertex and normal as coordinates in the (u, v, n) basis (C++ STriangle::Transform).

STrimBy.text: STrimBy records which sub-range of an SCurve trims this surface.

ShellGroup.text: ShellGroup is what the revolution constructors read from the group they build a shell for (C++ passes its Group): the faces of the new surfaces are entities from the group's remap table.

SurfaceCombineAs.text: SurfaceCombineAs is the boolean operation selector used by SSurface::MakeFromBoolean and the SShell/SMesh constructors that take a combine type.

String.text: String implements fmt.Stringer for debug logging.

SweepStep.text: SweepStep is one piece of a sweep's path: a translation by Along, or, with Arc, a turn by Angle radians about the axis through Center along Axis, by the right-hand rule.

Motion.text: Motion is the rigid motion of the step.

ApproxEqualGeometry.decl: func ApproxEqualGeometry(a, b *SEdgeList, tol float64) bool
ApproxEqualGeometry.text: ApproxEqualGeometry reports whether two SEdgeLists describe the same set of edges within tol.

CheckNormalAxisRelationship.decl: func CheckNormalAxisRelationship(sbls *SBezierLoopSet, pt, axis geom.Vector, da, dx float64) bool
CheckNormalAxisRelationship.text: CheckNormalAxisRelationship reports whether the direction of revolution/extrusion ends up parallel to the normal of the sketch, on the side of the axis where the sketch is.

ChordTolMm.text: ChordTolMm returns the absolute chord tolerance in mm: the export one in export mode (C++ SS.ChordTolMm).

CombineAsFromGroup.text: CombineAsFromGroup converts a sketch.Group::CombineAs into a SurfaceCombineAs.

CxxSort.decl: func CxxSort[T any](s []T, less func(a, b *T) bool)
CxxSort.text: CxxSort sorts s as libstdc++'s std::sort does, so that elements that compare equal end up in the same order as in C++ (std::sort isn't stable, and a mesh's order is what gets exported): introsort with a median-of-three pivot, heapsort past the depth limit, then insertion sort (bits/stl_algo.h, bits/stl_heap.h).

DoBounding.text: DoBounding extends (vmax, vmin) to include v (C++ SMesh::DoBounding).

ExportMode.text: ExportMode reports whether export mode is on.

FromExtrusionOf.decl: func FromExtrusionOf(spc *SBezier, t0, t1 geom.Vector) SSurface
FromExtrusionOf.text: FromExtrusionOf builds a surface by extruding a Bezier profile from t0 to t1.

FromPlane.decl: func FromPlane(pt, u, v geom.Vector) SSurface
FromPlane.text: FromPlane builds a planar surface of degree (1, 1) with normal u×v at point pt.

FromRevolutionOf.decl: func FromRevolutionOf(sb *SBezier, pt, axis geom.Vector, thetas, thetaf, dists, distf float64) SSurface
FromRevolutionOf.text: FromRevolutionOf builds a surface by revolving a Bezier profile around an axis (pt, axis) over the angular range [thetas, thetaf], with optional endpoint shrinkage distances (dists, distf).

FromTransformationOf.decl: func FromTransformationOf(a *SSurface, t geom.Vector, q geom.Quaternion, scale float64, includingTrims bool) SSurface
FromTransformationOf.text: FromTransformationOf produces a transformed copy of the surface.

FromTransformationOfSCurve.decl: func FromTransformationOfSCurve(a *SCurve, t geom.Vector, q geom.Quaternion, scale float64) SCurve
FromTransformationOfSCurve.text: FromTransformationOfSCurve is a copy of a scaled, then rotated, then translated; like C++ it keeps only the handle, the exact form, the surfaces and the pwl (C++ SCurve::FromTransformationOf).

GetMaxSegments.text: GetMaxSegments returns the maximum number of pwl segments per curve: the export one in export mode (C++ SS.GetMaxSegments).

NewMeshMeta.decl: func NewMeshMeta(face FaceID, color core.RgbaColor) MeshMeta
NewMeshMeta.text: NewMeshMeta constructs a MeshMeta with the given face id and color.

NewSTriMeta.decl: func NewSTriMeta(face FaceID, color core.RgbaColor) STriMeta
NewSTriMeta.text: NewSTriMeta constructs an STriMeta with the given face id and color.

OriginFor.decl: func OriginFor(g uint32, i int) uint32
OriginFor.text: OriginFor is the Origin of surface i of the surfaces group g made: bit 30 set, which no entity handle a sketch makes has, then the group's handle and i.

PolygonLoopSet.text: PolygonLoopSet is the closed polygon through pts, which lie in a plane with normal n, as a loop set for the shell constructors: an outer loop of lines wound clockwise about n, as FindOuterFacesFrom leaves outer loops.

ProbeTangentFace.decl: func ProbeTangentFace(srf *SSurface, p, interEdgeN, nu geom.Vector, f *geom.Vector, flat *bool) float64
ProbeTangentFace.text: ProbeTangentFace probes a face that meets the surface being classified tangentially at a point.

RayIsInside.decl: func RayIsInside(a, c, b, d geom.Vector) bool
RayIsInside.text: RayIsInside tests if ray b->d passes through triangle a,b,c.

SBezierFrom2.text: SBezierFrom2 builds a line segment from a to b.

SBezierFrom3.decl: func SBezierFrom3(a, b, c geom.Vector) SBezier
SBezierFrom3.text: SBezierFrom3 builds a quadratic Bezier from three control points.

SBezierFrom4.decl: func SBezierFrom4(a, b, c, d geom.Vector) SBezier
SBezierFrom4.text: SBezierFrom4 builds a cubic Bezier from four control points.

SBezierFromV4.text: SBezierFromV4 is the curve with homogeneous control points ct (C++ SBezier::From(Vector4 ...)).

SBezierLoopFromCurves.text: SBezierLoopFromCurves removes curves from sbl, chaining them end-to-start (reversing a curve when needed) into one loop.

SBsp2InsertOrCreateEdge.decl: func SBsp2InsertOrCreateEdge(where *SBsp2, nedge *SEdge, nnp, out geom.Vector) *SBsp2
SBsp2InsertOrCreateEdge.text: SBsp2InsertOrCreateEdge inserts nedge into the tree at where, making a node of it if the tree ends there (C++ SBsp2::InsertOrCreateEdge).

SBsp3FromMesh.text: SBsp3FromMesh builds the BSP of mesh m, inserting its triangles in the shuffled order C++ does (C++ SBsp3::FromMesh).

SBsp3InsertOrCreate.text: SBsp3InsertOrCreate inserts tr into the tree at where, making a node of it if the tree ends there; with instead, the triangle instead goes into (or is discarded from) that mesh (C++ SBsp3::InsertOrCreate).

SBspUvFrom.text: SBspUvFrom builds a BSP from the uv-space edge list el (points stored in the X/Y components).

SKdNodeEdgesFrom.text: SKdNodeEdgesFrom builds the tree over the edges of sel, which it keeps pointers into (C++ SKdNodeEdges::From(SEdgeList *)).

SKdNodeFrom.text: SKdNodeFrom builds the kd-tree over copies of mesh m's triangles, in the shuffled order C++ gives them (C++ SKdNode::From(SMesh *)).

STriangleFrom.decl: func STriangleFrom(meta STriMeta, a, b, c geom.Vector) STriangle
STriangleFrom.text: STriangleFrom is a triangle with the given vertices, and zero vertex normals (C++ STriangle::From).

STrimByEntireCurveFromShell.decl: func STrimByEntireCurveFromShell(shell *SShell, hsc core.HSCurve, backwards bool) STrimBy

SetChordTolMm.text: SetChordTolMm sets the absolute chord tolerance in mm.

SetExportMode.decl: func SetExportMode(on bool, chordTolMm float64, maxSegments int)
SetExportMode.text: SetExportMode turns export mode on, with the given chord tolerance in mm and segment limit, or off (C++ SS.exportMode).

SetMaxSegments.text: SetMaxSegments sets the maximum number of pwl segments per curve outside export mode (C++ SS.maxSegments).

SetParallelMode.text: SetParallelMode sets the mode; like the chord tolerance, not while a sketch is generated.

SetParallelModeFromEnv.text: SetParallelModeFromEnv takes SPACESOLVE_PARALLEL: "exact" (the default) has the solids generated on all the processors where that gives the bits of one; "fast" on all of them throughout, for other last bits; "off" on one.

SweepEnd.text: SweepEnd is where the steps take the profile.

TransformedLoopSet.text: TransformedLoopSet is a copy of sbls moved by r.

DotProductTol.text: DotProductTol is the direction-cosine tolerance used to decide whether two normals are perpendicular (in shell classification).

io.name: io
io.text: Package io provides basic interfaces to I/O primitives.

ByteReader.text: ByteReader is the interface that wraps the ReadByte method.

ByteScanner.text: ByteScanner is the interface that adds the UnreadByte method to the basic ReadByte method.

ByteWriter.text: ByteWriter is the interface that wraps the WriteByte method.

Closer.text: Closer is the interface that wraps the basic Close method.

LimitedReader.text: A LimitedReader reads from R but limits the amount of data returned to just N bytes.

OffsetWriter.text: An OffsetWriter maps writes at offset base to offset base+off in the underlying writer.

Seek.decl: func (o *OffsetWriter) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)

WriteAt.decl: func (o *OffsetWriter) WriteAt(p []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)

PipeReader.text: A PipeReader is the read half of a pipe.

Close.text: Close closes the reader; subsequent writes to the write half of the pipe will return the error ErrClosedPipe.

CloseWithError.text: CloseWithError closes the reader; subsequent writes to the write half of the pipe will return the error err.

Read.text: Read implements the standard Read interface: it reads data from the pipe, blocking until a writer arrives or the write end is closed.

PipeWriter.text: A PipeWriter is the write half of a pipe.

Close.text: Close closes the writer; subsequent reads from the read half of the pipe will return no bytes and EOF.

CloseWithError.text: CloseWithError closes the writer; subsequent reads from the read half of the pipe will return no bytes and the error err, or EOF if err is nil.

Write.text: Write implements the standard Write interface: it writes data to the pipe, blocking until one or more readers have consumed all the data or the read end is closed.

ReadCloser.text: ReadCloser is the interface that groups the basic Read and Close methods.

ReadSeekCloser.text: ReadSeekCloser is the interface that groups the basic Read, Seek and Close methods.

ReadSeeker.text: ReadSeeker is the interface that groups the basic Read and Seek methods.

ReadWriteCloser.text: ReadWriteCloser is the interface that groups the basic Read, Write and Close methods.

ReadWriteSeeker.text: ReadWriteSeeker is the interface that groups the basic Read, Write and Seek methods.

ReadWriter.text: ReadWriter is the interface that groups the basic Read and Write methods.

Reader.text: Reader is the interface that wraps the basic Read method.

ReaderAt.text: ReaderAt is the interface that wraps the basic ReadAt method.

ReaderFrom.text: ReaderFrom is the interface that wraps the ReadFrom method.

RuneReader.text: RuneReader is the interface that wraps the ReadRune method.

RuneScanner.text: RuneScanner is the interface that adds the UnreadRune method to the basic ReadRune method.

SectionReader.text: SectionReader implements Read, Seek, and ReadAt on a section of an underlying ReaderAt.

Outer.decl: func (s *SectionReader) Outer() (r ReaderAt, off int64, n int64)
Outer.text: Outer returns the underlying ReaderAt and offsets for the section.

ReadAt.decl: func (s *SectionReader) ReadAt(p []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)

Seek.decl: func (s *SectionReader) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)

Size.text: Size returns the size of the section in bytes.

Seeker.text: Seeker is the interface that wraps the basic Seek method.

StringWriter.text: StringWriter is the interface that wraps the WriteString method.

WriteCloser.text: WriteCloser is the interface that groups the basic Write and Close methods.

WriteSeeker.text: WriteSeeker is the interface that groups the basic Write and Seek methods.

Writer.text: Writer is the interface that wraps the basic Write method.

WriterAt.text: WriterAt is the interface that wraps the basic WriteAt method.

WriterTo.text: WriterTo is the interface that wraps the WriteTo method.

Copy.decl: func Copy(dst Writer, src Reader) (written int64, err error)
Copy.text: Copy copies from src to dst until either EOF is reached on src or an error occurs.

CopyBuffer.decl: func CopyBuffer(dst Writer, src Reader, buf []byte) (written int64, err error)
CopyBuffer.text: CopyBuffer is identical to Copy except that it stages through the provided buffer (if one is required) rather than allocating a temporary one.

CopyN.decl: func CopyN(dst Writer, src Reader, n int64) (written int64, err error)
CopyN.text: CopyN copies n bytes (or until an error) from src to dst.

LimitReader.decl: func LimitReader(r Reader, n int64) Reader
LimitReader.text: LimitReader returns a Reader that reads from r but stops with EOF after n bytes.

MultiReader.text: MultiReader returns a Reader that's the logical concatenation of the provided input readers.

MultiWriter.text: MultiWriter creates a writer that duplicates its writes to all the provided writers, similar to the Unix tee(1) command.

NewOffsetWriter.text: NewOffsetWriter returns an OffsetWriter that writes to w starting at offset off.

NewSectionReader.decl: func NewSectionReader(r ReaderAt, off int64, n int64) *SectionReader
NewSectionReader.text: NewSectionReader returns a SectionReader that reads from r starting at offset off and stops with EOF after n bytes.

NopCloser.text: NopCloser returns a ReadCloser with a no-op Close method wrapping the provided Reader r.

Pipe.text: Pipe creates a synchronous in-memory pipe.

ReadAll.text: ReadAll reads from r until an error or EOF and returns the data it read.

ReadAtLeast.decl: func ReadAtLeast(r Reader, buf []byte, min int) (n int, err error)
ReadAtLeast.text: ReadAtLeast reads from r into buf until it has read at least min bytes.

ReadFull.decl: func ReadFull(r Reader, buf []byte) (n int, err error)
ReadFull.text: ReadFull reads exactly len(buf) bytes from r into buf.

TeeReader.decl: func TeeReader(r Reader, w Writer) Reader
TeeReader.text: TeeReader returns a Reader that writes to w what it reads from r.

WriteString.decl: func WriteString(w Writer, s string) (n int, err error)
WriteString.text: WriteString writes the contents of the string s to w, which accepts a slice of bytes.

Discard.text: Discard is a Writer on which all Write calls succeed without doing anything.

EOF.text: EOF is the error returned by Read when no more input is available.

ErrClosedPipe.text: ErrClosedPipe is the error used for read or write operations on a closed pipe.

ErrNoProgress.text: ErrNoProgress is returned by some clients of a Reader when many calls to Read have failed to return any data or error, usually the sign of a broken Reader implementation.

ErrShortBuffer.text: ErrShortBuffer means that a read required a longer buffer than was provided.

ErrShortWrite.text: ErrShortWrite means that a write accepted fewer bytes than requested but failed to return an explicit error.

ErrUnexpectedEOF.text: ErrUnexpectedEOF means that EOF was encountered in the middle of reading a fixed-size block or data structure.

io/fs.name: fs
io/fs.text: Package fs defines basic interfaces to a file system.

DirEntry.text: A DirEntry is an entry read from a directory (using the ReadDir function or a ReadDirFile's ReadDir method).

FS.text: An FS provides access to a hierarchical file system.

File.text: A File provides access to a single file.

FileInfo.text: A FileInfo describes a file and is returned by Stat.

FileMode.text: A FileMode represents a file's mode and permission bits.

IsDir.text: IsDir reports whether m describes a directory.

IsRegular.text: IsRegular reports whether m describes a regular file.

Perm.text: Perm returns the Unix permission bits in m (m & ModePerm).

Type.text: Type returns type bits in m (m & ModeType).

GlobFS.text: A GlobFS is a file system with a Glob method.

PathError.text: PathError records an error and the operation and file path that caused it.

Timeout.text: Timeout reports whether this error represents a timeout.

ReadDirFS.text: ReadDirFS is the interface implemented by a file system that provides an optimized implementation of ReadDir.

ReadDirFile.text: A ReadDirFile is a directory file whose entries can be read with the ReadDir method.

ReadFileFS.text: ReadFileFS is the interface implemented by a file system that provides an optimized implementation of ReadFile.

ReadLinkFS.text: ReadLinkFS is the interface implemented by a file system that supports reading symbolic links.

StatFS.text: A StatFS is a file system with a Stat method.

SubFS.text: A SubFS is a file system with a Sub method.

WalkDirFunc.text: WalkDirFunc is the type of the function called by WalkDir to visit each file or directory.

FileInfoToDirEntry.text: FileInfoToDirEntry returns a DirEntry that returns information from info.

FormatDirEntry.text: FormatDirEntry returns a formatted version of dir for human readability.

FormatFileInfo.text: FormatFileInfo returns a formatted version of info for human readability.

Glob.decl: func Glob(fsys FS, pattern string) (matches []string, err error)
Glob.text: Glob returns the names of all files matching pattern or nil if there is no matching file.

Lstat.decl: func Lstat(fsys FS, name string) (FileInfo, error)
Lstat.text: Lstat returns a FileInfo describing the named file.

ReadDir.decl: func ReadDir(fsys FS, name string) ([]DirEntry, error)
ReadDir.text: ReadDir reads the named directory and returns a list of directory entries sorted by filename.

ReadFile.decl: func ReadFile(fsys FS, name string) ([]byte, error)
ReadFile.text: ReadFile reads the named file from the file system fsys and returns its contents.

ReadLink.decl: func ReadLink(fsys FS, name string) (string, error)
ReadLink.text: ReadLink returns the destination of the named symbolic link.

Stat.decl: func Stat(fsys FS, name string) (FileInfo, error)
Stat.text: Stat returns a FileInfo describing the named file from the file system.

Sub.decl: func Sub(fsys FS, dir string) (FS, error)
Sub.text: Sub returns an FS corresponding to the subtree rooted at fsys's dir.

ValidPath.text: ValidPath reports whether the given path name is valid for use in a call to Open.

WalkDir.decl: func WalkDir(fsys FS, root string, fn WalkDirFunc) error
WalkDir.text: WalkDir walks the file tree rooted at root, calling fn for each file or directory in the tree, including root.

ErrClosed.text: ErrClosed is returned when operations are attempted on a file that has already been closed, including when Close is called more than once.

ModeAppend.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeCharDevice.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeDevice.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeDir.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeExclusive.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeIrregular.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeNamedPipe.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModePerm.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeSetgid.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeSetuid.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeSocket.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeSticky.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeSymlink.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeTemporary.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

ModeType.text: The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the FileMode.

SkipAll.text: SkipAll is used as a return value from WalkDirFunc to indicate that all remaining files and directories are to be skipped.

SkipDir.text: SkipDir is used as a return value from WalkDirFunc to indicate that the directory named in the call is to be skipped.

math.name: math
math.text: Package math provides basic constants and mathematical functions.

Abs.text: Abs returns the absolute value of x.

Acos.text: Acos returns the arccosine, in radians, of x.

Acosh.text: Acosh returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of x.

Asin.text: Asin returns the arcsine, in radians, of x.

Asinh.text: Asinh returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of x.

Atan.text: Atan returns the arctangent, in radians, of x.

Atan2.text: Atan2 returns the arc tangent of y/x, using the signs of the two to determine the quadrant of the return value.

Atanh.text: Atanh returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of x.

Cbrt.text: Cbrt returns the cube root of x.

Ceil.text: Ceil returns the least integer value greater than or equal to x.

Copysign.text: Copysign returns a value with the magnitude of f and the sign of sign.

Cos.text: Cos returns the cosine of the radian argument x.

Cosh.text: Cosh returns the hyperbolic cosine of x.

Dim.text: Dim returns the maximum of x-y or 0.

Erf.text: Erf returns the error function of x.

Erfc.text: Erfc returns the complementary error function of x.

Erfcinv.text: Erfcinv returns the inverse of Erfc(x).

Erfinv.text: Erfinv returns the inverse error function of x.

Exp.text: Exp returns e**x, the base-e exponential of x.

Exp2.text: Exp2 returns 2**x, the base-2 exponential of x.

Expm1.text: Expm1 returns e**x - 1, the base-e exponential of x minus 1.

FMA.decl: func FMA(x, y, z float64) float64
FMA.text: FMA returns x * y + z, computed with only one rounding.

Float32bits.text: Float32bits returns the IEEE 754 binary representation of f, with the sign bit of f and the result in the same bit position.

Float32frombits.text: Float32frombits returns the floating-point number corresponding to the IEEE 754 binary representation b, with the sign bit of b and the result in the same bit position.

Float64bits.text: Float64bits returns the IEEE 754 binary representation of f, with the sign bit of f and the result in the same bit position, and Float64bits(Float64frombits(x)) == x.

Float64frombits.text: Float64frombits returns the floating-point number corresponding to the IEEE 754 binary representation b, with the sign bit of b and the result in the same bit position.

Floor.text: Floor returns the greatest integer value less than or equal to x.

Frexp.decl: func Frexp(f float64) (frac float64, exp int)
Frexp.text: Frexp breaks f into a normalized fraction and an integral power of two.

Gamma.text: Gamma returns the Gamma function of x.

Hypot.text: Hypot returns Sqrt(p*p + q*q), taking care to avoid unnecessary overflow and underflow.

Ilogb.text: Ilogb returns the binary exponent of x as an integer.

Inf.text: Inf returns positive infinity if sign >= 0, negative infinity if sign < 0.

IsInf.decl: func IsInf(f float64, sign int) bool
IsInf.text: IsInf reports whether f is an infinity, according to sign.

IsNaN.text: IsNaN reports whether f is an IEEE 754 “not-a-number” value.

J0.text: J0 returns the order-zero Bessel function of the first kind.

J1.text: J1 returns the order-one Bessel function of the first kind.

Jn.decl: func Jn(n int, x float64) float64
Jn.text: Jn returns the order-n Bessel function of the first kind.

Ldexp.decl: func Ldexp(frac float64, exp int) float64
Ldexp.text: Ldexp is the inverse of Frexp.

Lgamma.decl: func Lgamma(x float64) (lgamma float64, sign int)
Lgamma.text: Lgamma returns the natural logarithm and sign (-1 or +1) of Gamma(x).

Log.text: Log returns the natural logarithm of x.

Log10.text: Log10 returns the decimal logarithm of x.

Log1p.text: Log1p returns the natural logarithm of 1 plus its argument x.

Log2.text: Log2 returns the binary logarithm of x.

Logb.text: Logb returns the binary exponent of x.

Max.text: Max returns the larger of x or y.

Min.text: Min returns the smaller of x or y.

Mod.text: Mod returns the floating-point remainder of x/y.

Modf.decl: func Modf(f float64) (integer float64, fractional float64)
Modf.text: Modf returns integer and fractional floating-point numbers that sum to f.

Nextafter.text: Nextafter returns the next representable float64 value after x towards y.

Nextafter32.text: Nextafter32 returns the next representable float32 value after x towards y.

Pow.text: Pow returns x**y, the base-x exponential of y.

Pow10.text: Pow10 returns 10**n, the base-10 exponential of n.

Remainder.text: Remainder returns the IEEE 754 floating-point remainder of x/y.

Round.text: Round returns the nearest integer, rounding half away from zero.

RoundToEven.text: RoundToEven returns the nearest integer, rounding ties to even.

Signbit.text: Signbit reports whether x is negative or negative zero.

Sin.text: Sin returns the sine of the radian argument x.

Sinh.text: Sinh returns the hyperbolic sine of x.

Sqrt.text: Sqrt returns the square root of x.

Tan.text: Tan returns the tangent of the radian argument x.

Tanh.text: Tanh returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.

Trunc.text: Trunc returns the integer value of x.

Y0.text: Y0 returns the order-zero Bessel function of the second kind.

Y1.text: Y1 returns the order-one Bessel function of the second kind.

Yn.decl: func Yn(n int, x float64) float64
Yn.text: Yn returns the order-n Bessel function of the second kind.

math/bits.name: bits
math/bits.text: Package bits implements bit counting and manipulation functions for the predeclared unsigned integer types.

Add.decl: func Add(x, y, carry uint) (sum, carryOut uint)
Add.text: Add returns the sum with carry of x, y and carry: sum = x + y + carry.

Add32.decl: func Add32(x, y, carry uint32) (sum, carryOut uint32)
Add32.text: Add32 returns the sum with carry of x, y and carry: sum = x + y + carry.

Add64.decl: func Add64(x, y, carry uint64) (sum, carryOut uint64)
Add64.text: Add64 returns the sum with carry of x, y and carry: sum = x + y + carry.

Div.decl: func Div(hi, lo, y uint) (quo, rem uint)
Div.text: Div returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y: quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.

Div32.decl: func Div32(hi, lo, y uint32) (quo, rem uint32)
Div32.text: Div32 returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y: quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.

Div64.decl: func Div64(hi, lo, y uint64) (quo, rem uint64)
Div64.text: Div64 returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y: quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.

LeadingZeros.text: LeadingZeros returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is UintSize for x == 0.

LeadingZeros16.text: LeadingZeros16 returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is 16 for x == 0.

LeadingZeros32.text: LeadingZeros32 returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is 32 for x == 0.

LeadingZeros64.text: LeadingZeros64 returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is 64 for x == 0.

LeadingZeros8.text: LeadingZeros8 returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is 8 for x == 0.

Len.text: Len returns the minimum number of bits required to represent x; the result is 0 for x == 0.

Len16.text: Len16 returns the minimum number of bits required to represent x; the result is 0 for x == 0.

Len32.text: Len32 returns the minimum number of bits required to represent x; the result is 0 for x == 0.

Len64.text: Len64 returns the minimum number of bits required to represent x; the result is 0 for x == 0.

Len8.text: Len8 returns the minimum number of bits required to represent x; the result is 0 for x == 0.

Mul.decl: func Mul(x, y uint) (hi, lo uint)
Mul.text: Mul returns the full-width product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower half returned in lo.

Mul32.decl: func Mul32(x, y uint32) (hi, lo uint32)
Mul32.text: Mul32 returns the 64-bit product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower half returned in lo.

Mul64.decl: func Mul64(x, y uint64) (hi, lo uint64)
Mul64.text: Mul64 returns the 128-bit product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower half returned in lo.

OnesCount.text: OnesCount returns the number of one bits ("population count") in x.

OnesCount16.text: OnesCount16 returns the number of one bits ("population count") in x.

OnesCount32.text: OnesCount32 returns the number of one bits ("population count") in x.

OnesCount64.text: OnesCount64 returns the number of one bits ("population count") in x.

OnesCount8.text: OnesCount8 returns the number of one bits ("population count") in x.

Rem.decl: func Rem(hi, lo, y uint) uint
Rem.text: Rem returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y.

Rem32.decl: func Rem32(hi, lo, y uint32) uint32
Rem32.text: Rem32 returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y.

Rem64.decl: func Rem64(hi, lo, y uint64) uint64
Rem64.text: Rem64 returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y.

Reverse16.text: Reverse16 returns the value of x with its bits in reversed order.

Reverse32.text: Reverse32 returns the value of x with its bits in reversed order.

ReverseBytes64.text: ReverseBytes64 returns the value of x with its bytes in reversed order.

RotateLeft.decl: func RotateLeft(x uint, k int) uint
RotateLeft.text: RotateLeft returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod UintSize) bits.

RotateLeft16.decl: func RotateLeft16(x uint16, k int) uint16
RotateLeft16.text: RotateLeft16 returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod 16) bits.

RotateLeft32.decl: func RotateLeft32(x uint32, k int) uint32
RotateLeft32.text: RotateLeft32 returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod 32) bits.

RotateLeft64.decl: func RotateLeft64(x uint64, k int) uint64
RotateLeft64.text: RotateLeft64 returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod 64) bits.

RotateLeft8.decl: func RotateLeft8(x uint8, k int) uint8
RotateLeft8.text: RotateLeft8 returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod 8) bits.

math/rand.name: rand
math/rand.text: Package rand implements pseudo-random number generators suitable for tasks such as simulation, but it should not be used for security-sensitive work.

Rand.text: A Rand is a source of random numbers.

ExpFloat64.text: ExpFloat64 returns an exponentially distributed float64 in the range (0, +[math.MaxFloat64]] with an exponential distribution whose rate parameter (lambda) is 1 and whose mean is 1/lambda (1).

Float32.text: Float32 returns, as a float32, a pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0.0,1.0).

Float64.text: Float64 returns, as a float64, a pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0.0,1.0).

Int.text: Int returns a non-negative pseudo-random int.

Int31.text: Int31 returns a non-negative pseudo-random 31-bit integer as an int32.

Int31n.text: Int31n returns, as an int32, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n).

Int63.text: Int63 returns a non-negative pseudo-random 63-bit integer as an int64.

Int63n.text: Int63n returns, as an int64, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n).

Intn.text: Intn returns, as an int, a non-negative pseudo-random number in the half-open interval [0,n).

NormFloat64.text: NormFloat64 returns a normally distributed float64 in the range -math.MaxFloat64 through +[math.MaxFloat64] inclusive, with standard normal distribution (mean = 0, stddev = 1).

Perm.text: Perm returns, as a slice of n ints, a pseudo-random permutation of the integers in the half-open interval [0,n).

Read.text: Read generates len(p) random bytes and writes them into p.

Seed.text: Seed uses the provided seed value to initialize the generator to a deterministic state.

Shuffle.decl: func (r *Rand) Shuffle(n int, swap func(i, j int))
Shuffle.text: Shuffle pseudo-randomizes the order of elements.

Uint32.text: Uint32 returns a pseudo-random 32-bit value as a uint32.

Uint64.text: Uint64 returns a pseudo-random 64-bit value as a uint64.

Source.text: A Source represents a source of uniformly-distributed pseudo-random int64 values in the range [0, 1<<63).

Source64.text: A Source64 is a Source that can also generate uniformly-distributed pseudo-random uint64 values in the range [0, 1<<64) directly.

Zipf.text: A Zipf generates Zipf distributed variates.

Uint64.text: Uint64 returns a value drawn from the Zipf distribution described by the Zipf object.
